+actions in one transaction (LLP 3000.039 §3). A live restrict child or physical
+read-through child may retain the root physically, but the expired root remains
+absent from all logical reads. Cleanup advances past such retained roots and
+preserves its bounded scan position across calls; cascade/set-null writes and
+the root removal either commit together or roll back together. The same action
+path governs a row born expired at commit and an expired predecessor retired
+for a same-id insertion, so neither inline cleanup path can create an orphan.
+
+Expiring a never-opened root creates no root deletion event, because no device
+could hold it. Its actions can still change opened children, and those ordinary
+row changes carry their partition events. Deleting an opened row keeps the

+at the case clock, while physical write lookup and uniqueness remain over stored
+rows. The emitter includes both fields. The model's explicit physical sweep
+uses the same cascade/restrict/set-null closure as delete, retains a restricted
+root and continues to later due rows. The Lean difftest generator preserves
+seeded expiry values and requested prelude/final sweeps, advances the formal
+store with each engine sweep, then compares the following program outcome.
 
 The difftest AST and generator produce null/past/future/equal-boundary openings,
 opening plus expiry, membership witnesses and caps. Its first formal fragment

@@ -262,10 +262,25 @@ Every step is inside the mutation's transaction: a refusal anywhere (a

-**Expiry is not a delete.** A parent whose `expire at` passes is absent from
-that moment, and the sweep removes it physically; neither fires an action.
-A child of an expiring parent outlives it unless the child declares the same
-lifetime (`read through`, or its own `expire at`). The writes card says so.
+**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
+is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
+can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
+sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
+expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
+bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
+not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
+constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
+
+A live `restrict` child keeps the expired root physically stored and the sweep
+continues to later due keys. The retained root remains logically unreadable.
+Short sweeps preserve a per-table scan continuation, so repeated bounded calls
+cannot restart forever at the same restricted or read-through-retained roots;
+after reaching the end they wrap for roots whose blockers were removed.
+Expired children are not live restrict witnesses, as in step 4. A read-through
+child remains the stricter physical exception because its stored image depends
+on its parent. Any error after an earlier cascade or set-null write rolls back
+the whole retirement transaction. A restricted root alone is an expected
+deferred cleanup, not an error for the sweep as a whole.

+/// Activation marker for the maintained-row address function. A missing or

+pub const MAINTAINED_ID_META: &str = "maintained_id_version";
+pub const MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION: &str = "sha256-v1";
+
+/// The id of a maintained row is a fixed-size digest of its typed group key.
+/// Programs address aggregates by their group index, never by this internal

+#[test]
+fn maintained_identity_is_fixed_size_and_domain_separated() {
+    let short = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".into())]);
+    let long = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".repeat(100_000))]);
+    assert_eq!(short.len(), 64);
+    assert_eq!(long.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(short, long);
+    assert_ne!(short, crate::value::digest(&[Value::String("x".into())]));

+#[test]
+fn missing_identity_marker_rebuilds_a_principal_reference_and_max_text_group() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table parents:\n  public\ntable entries:\n  owner: principal\n  parent: parents\n  token: text <=64\n  amount: int\n  public\nview totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token\n  public\n";
+    let initial = compile(SOURCE);
+    let mut e = Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), initial.schema, initial.programs, 0).unwrap();
+    let owner = format!("user:{}", "o".repeat(59));
+    let parent = "p".repeat(64);
+    let token = "t".repeat(64);
+    assert_eq!((owner.len(), parent.len(), token.len()), (64, 64, 64));
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("parents".into(), object([("id", Value::Id(parent.clone()))])),
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("owner", Value::Id(owner.clone())),
+            ("parent", Value::Id(parent.clone())), ("token", Value::String(token.clone())), ("amount", Value::Int(7))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(owner), Value::Id(parent), Value::String(token)]);
+    let before = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(before.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+    assert_eq!(expected.len(), 64);
+
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    assert_eq!(preview(&mut e, &next.schema).aggregate_rows, 1);
+    let generation = e.generation();
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.generation() > generation);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+    let after = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(after.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn identity_redeployment_rebuilds_the_ungrouped_empty_tuple() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  public\nview total: count entries\n  public\n";
+    let initial = compile(SOURCE);
+    let mut e = Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), initial.schema, initial.programs, 0).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into()))]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[]);
+    let before = e.store().rows("total").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(before.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("$global").unwrap(), &Value::Bool(true));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    assert_eq!(preview(&mut e, &next.schema).aggregate_rows, 1);
+    let generation = e.generation();
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.generation() > generation);
+    let after = e.store().rows("total").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(after.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("$global").unwrap(), &Value::Bool(true));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+}

+#[test]
+fn aggregate_identity_capability_upgrades_legacy_wire_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let schema = compile("table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n");
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    // A pre-migration stored schema may already have a carrier for unrelated
+    // capabilities. Decode it once, then stamp the digest identity capability
+    // on every newly published schema/projection.
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();
+    for table in legacy["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let upgraded: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy).unwrap();
+    let encoded = serde_json::to_string(&upgraded).unwrap();
+    assert!(encoded.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    let required = snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&upgraded.public_projection());
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities.retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"), "{refusal:?}");
+}
+

+  sync public
+table cascadeChildren:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  public 'cascadeChildren'
+  sync public

+#[test]
+fn authoritative_memory_sweeps_resume_and_wrap_past_restricted_roots() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+"#;
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let mut store = snapback4_device::memory::MemoryStore::new();
+    store.activate_server_at(bound.schema, 0).unwrap();
+    store.seed_server_at([
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "continuation reaches the free root within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(store.raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(store.raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("root").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+
+    // The cursor is after z. A lower new key is found after the scan wraps;
+    // each restricted root still consumes one bounded visit.
+    store.seed_server_at([("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", id("aa-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10)),
+    ]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "a wrapped scan reaches the new lower key within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(!store.raw_rows("roots").iter().any(|row| row.field("id").unwrap() == &id("aa-free")));
+}

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..05a91f6ddf
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+//! Expiry is a physical delete trigger for referential actions (LLP 3000.039
+//! §3). These cases cover scheduled cleanup, commit-end retirement and
+//! same-id replacement of an expired row against the real engine.
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState, value::object};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn id(value: &str) -> Value { Value::Id(value.into()) }
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+const SWEEP: &str = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+  sync public
+"#;
+
+#[test]
+fn sweep_applies_every_action_and_advances_past_a_restricted_root() {
+    let mut e = engine(SWEEP);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("ca")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    for expected in [0, 0, 0, 1] {
+        assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), expected, "a one-row sweep must advance its physical scan position");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["a-blocked", "b-blocked", "c-blocked"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["ca"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    for blocker in ["ba", "bb", "bc"] { e.seed_delete("blockers", blocker).unwrap(); }
+    assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap(), 3);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_late_cascade_refusal_rolls_back_earlier_set_null_writes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'children'
+table grandchildren:
+  child: children
+  read through .child
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("n")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("c")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("grandchildren".into(), object([("id", id("g")), ("child", id("c"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    let error = e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", "{error:?}");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &id("p"), "the prior set-null write rolled back");
+    for table in ["roots", "children", "grandchildren"] {
+        assert_eq!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().len(), 1, "{table}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn commit_retirement_and_expired_same_id_replacement_apply_actions() {
+    let source = format!(r#"{SWEEP}
+mutation bornExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'born', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert cascadeKids {{id: 'born-c', root: 'born'}}
+  insert nullableKids {{id: 'born-n', root: 'born'}}
+  return null
+mutation bornRestricted():
+  insert roots {{id: 'blocked', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert blockers {{id: 'blocked-b', root: 'blocked'}}
+  return null
+mutation replaceExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'old', expiresAt: null}}
+  return null
+"#);
+    let mut e = engine(&source);
+    let sent = e.mutate("bornExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    let refused = e.mutate("bornRestricted", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty(), "the refused birth and its blocker roll back together");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("blockers").unwrap().is_empty());
+
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(1))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("old-c")), ("root", id("old"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replaceExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("expiresAt").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty(), "same-id cleanup cannot orphan the expired predecessor's child");
+}
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c6754a981f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+//! A store written by the frozen 0.4.28 binary adopts digest-addressed
+//! aggregate rows before the current engine serves it.
+use rusqlite::Connection;
+use std::{
+    fs,
+    path::{Path, PathBuf},
+    process::Command,
+};
+
+const SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
+table entries:
+  group: text <=256
+  amount: int
+  insert <- allow
+  public
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .group
+  public
+mutation add(group: text <=256, amount: int):
+  insert entries {group, amount}
+query total(group: text <=256):
+  return totals[group]
+"#;
+
+struct Temp(PathBuf);
+impl Temp {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
+            "snapback4-maintained-id-{}-{}",
+            std::process::id(),
+            std::time::SystemTime::now()
+                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+                .unwrap()
+                .as_nanos()
+        ));
+        fs::create_dir_all(path.join("snapback")).unwrap();
+        fs::write(path.join("snapback/schema.q"), SOURCE).unwrap();
+        Self(path)
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for Temp {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
+    }
+}
+
+fn aggregate_id(store: &Path) -> String {
+    Connection::open(store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT r.id FROM r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t WHERE c.name='totals'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires frozen 0.4.28 binary via SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN"]
+fn a_0_4_28_store_rebuilds_legacy_aggregate_ids_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let baseline = PathBuf::from(
+        std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN")
+            .expect("set SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN to the frozen 0.4.28 snapback4 binary"),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        baseline.is_file(),
+        "SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN is not a file: {}",
+        baseline.display()
+    );
+    let version = Command::new(&baseline).arg("--version").output().unwrap();
+    assert!(version.status.success());
+    assert!(
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&version.stdout).contains("0.4.28"),
+        "unexpected baseline: {:?}",
+        version
+    );
+
+    let dir = Temp::new();
+    let group = "x".repeat(200);
+    let args = serde_json::json!({"group": group, "amount": 7}).to_string();
+    let written = Command::new(&baseline)
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args(["run", "add", &args, "--as", "alice", "--now", "1", "--json"])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        written.status.success(),
+        "{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&written.stderr)
+    );
+    let store = dir.0.join(".snapback4/store.sqlite");
+    let legacy = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert!(
+        legacy.len() > snapback4_core::rows::MAX_ID_BYTES,
+        "the frozen binary must have written the oversized legacy address"
+    );
+    let before: u64 = Connection::open(&store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap();
+
+    let opened = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_snapback4"))
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args([
+            "run",
+            "total",
+            &serde_json::json!({"group": group}).to_string(),
+            "--as",
+            "alice",
+            "--now",
+            "2",
+            "--json",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        opened.status.success(),
+        "stdout={} stderr={}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stderr)
+    );
+    let answer: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&opened.stdout).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(answer["data"]["value"], 7, "{answer}");
+
+    let digest = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert_eq!(digest.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(digest, legacy);
+    let conn = Connection::open(&store).unwrap();
+    let (after, marker): (u64, String) = (
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap(),
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+            [snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap(),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        after > before,
+        "identity adoption must publish a new device generation"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(marker, snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION);
+
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), SOURCE.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let required =
+        snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&bound.schema.public_projection());
+    assert!(
+        required
+            .capabilities
+            .contains(&"maintained-id-sha256-v1".to_owned())
+    );
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities
+        .retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(
+        refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"),
+        "{refusal:?}"
+    );
+}

    18	    pub(super) fn apply_reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

    59	    fn reference_closure(&mut self, root_table: &str, root: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

   143	    /// Streams the ids of the live rows referencing `id` through `r` to
   144	    /// `visit`, through its index, until `visit` answers false. A capped walk
   145	    /// (cascade, set null) reads `PAGE` rows per seek and holds at most the
   146	    /// reference's cap; a restrict probe reads one row per seek, so it examines
   147	    /// nothing past its witness. Images are dropped before `visit` runs. Seeks
   148	    /// start at the live suffix, so an expired backlog is never visited.
   149	    fn each_child(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value, capped: bool, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Self, Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   150	        let schema = self.schema;
   151	        let index = schema.reference_index(r.child, r.column).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} has no reference index", r.child, r.column)))?.to_owned();

   157	        } else {

   162	            let mut bounds = Bounds { gt, ..Default::default() };
   163	            loop {
   164	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, r.child, &index, &prefix, &bounds, Dir::Asc, page_rows))?;

   206	    /// The engine's own write of a `set null` reference: no rule, every constraint.
   207	    fn clear_reference(&mut self, table: &str, column: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   208	        let mut new = old.clone();

   213	            runner.reserve_maintains(table, &runner.schema.tables[table])?;

   220	    /// The engine's own delete of a closure row: no rule, its constraints, its
   221	    /// `read through` children's probe, maintains and partition events.
   222	    fn delete_reached(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   223	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   224	            runner.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;

   226	            runner.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;

   232	/// Rows a child scan holds per seek: the reservation's transient `4 × row`

   241	/// other reached table must be removed before it (the cascade and `read
   242	/// through` edges are acyclic by `check`), and within a table, later
   243	/// discoveries first.
   244	fn deletion_order(schema: &crate::schema::Schema, reached: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
   245	    let tables: Vec<&str> = {
   246	        let mut seen = Vec::new();
   247	        for (table, _) in reached { if !seen.contains(&table.as_str()) { seen.push(table.as_str()); } }
   248	        seen
   249	    };
   250	    // edges: child table -> the reached tables it must be removed before
   251	    // (its cascade parents and its `read through` parent; LLP 3000.039 §3).
   252	    let mut edges: Vec<(&str, &str)> = Vec::new();
   253	    for &child in &tables {
   254	        for &parent in &tables {
   255	            if child != parent && schema.deletion_precedes(child, parent) { edges.push((child, parent)); }
   256	        }
   257	    }
   258	    let mut order: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
   259	    let mut remaining = tables.clone();
   260	    while !remaining.is_empty() {
   261	        // A table no remaining table references can go now (its referencers are gone).
   262	        let position = remaining.iter().position(|t| !remaining.iter().any(|other| other != t && edges.contains(&(*other, *t))))

   267	    for table in order {
   268	        out.extend(reached.iter().rev().filter(|(t, _)| t == table).cloned());
   269	    }
   270	    out
   271	}

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs

index 0000000000..3708ad4a5a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
+//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
+//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
+use super::*;
+
+pub(super) fn install(
+    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
+    schema: &Schema,
+    creating: bool,
+    generation: u64,
+) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+    let current = tx.query(
+        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
+        &[],
+    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
+    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
+        return Ok(generation);
+    }
+
+    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
+        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
+        .cloned()
+        .collect();
+    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
+        let mut runner = Runner::new(
+            tx,
+            schema,
+            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
+            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
+            tx.next_seq()?,
+        );
+        runner.event_free = true;
+        for maintain in &aggregates {
+            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
+        }
+    }
+
+    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
+        generation
+    } else {
+        generation.checked_add(1)
+            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
+    };
+    tx.execute(
+        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
+        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
+    )?;
+    Ok(generation)
+}

+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires isolated local Postgres; scripts/test-postgres.sh"]
+fn reopening_legacy_maintained_ids_rebuilds_before_publishing_the_generation() {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), r#"
+table entries:
+  bucket: int
+  public
+view totals: count entries by .bucket
+  public
+"#.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let schema: Schema = serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(&bound.schema).unwrap()).unwrap();
+    let programs = bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program).collect::<Vec<_>>();
+    let url = std::env::var("SNAPBACK4_EVAL_POSTGRES").expect("private test-postgres.sh database");
+    let name = format!("sb4_eval_maintained_id_{:x}", crate::ids::seed());
+    let mut engine = PostgresEngine::create(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name, schema, programs).unwrap();
+    engine.load([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))]))]).unwrap();
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let target = engine.schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let generation = engine.generation();
+    let tx = engine.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized)).unwrap();
+    let old = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("current aggregate");
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
+    let mut old = old;
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut old {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &old, None).unwrap();
+    tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=NULL WHERE singleton", &[]).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    drop(engine);
+
+    let mut reopened = PostgresEngine::open(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(reopened.generation(), generation + 1);
+    let tx = reopened.store.transaction(None).unwrap();
+    assert!(tx.get("totals", &legacy).unwrap().is_none());
+    let rebuilt = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("digest aggregate");
+    assert_eq!(rebuilt.field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

+const EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR: &str = "$expiry-table";
+
+/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
+/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
+/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
+pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
+    mut tables: Vec<String>,
+    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
+) -> Vec<String> {
+    let after = cursors
+        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
+        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
+        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
+    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
+        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
+        tables.rotate_left(next);
+    }
+    tables
+}
+
+pub(crate) fn mark_expiry_table(cursors: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>, table: &str) {
+    cursors.insert(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR.into(), vec![Value::String(table.into())]);
+}

+/// The copied corpus is a frozen image of the pre-digest store. Translate
+/// maintained target identities at the adapter boundary so its logical values
+/// remain an oracle for the current address function. Other row ids retain
+/// their exact frozen spelling.
+fn legacy_maintained_ids(schema: &Schema, rows: &[ReceiptRow]) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, String> {
+    let mut ids = BTreeMap::new();
+    for receipt in rows {
+        let Some(maintain) = schema.maintains.iter().find(|maintain| maintain.target == receipt.table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) else { continue };
+        let old = match receipt.row.field("id") {
+            Ok(Value::Id(id)) => id,
+            Ok(_) => return Err(format!("{}.id is not an id", receipt.table)),
+            Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}.id: {error}", receipt.table)),
+        };
+        let key = maintain.by.iter().map(|field| receipt.row.field(field).cloned().map_err(|error| format!("{}.{}: {error}", receipt.table, field))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
+        let new = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        if let Some(prior) = ids.insert(old.clone(), new.clone())
+            && prior != new
+        {
+            return Err(format!("legacy id {old} names more than one maintained group"));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(ids)
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_row(schema: &Schema, table: &str, row: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    if !schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.target == table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) { return; }
+    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return };
+    let Some(Value::Id(id)) = fields.get_mut("id") else { return };
+    if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+        *id = replacement.clone();
+    }
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_expected(expected: &mut Expected, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<(), String> {
+    if ids.is_empty() || expected.error_code.is_some() { return Ok(()); }
+    let Some(canonical) = &expected.canonical_result else { return Ok(()) };
+    let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(canonical).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    translate_legacy_maintained_result(&mut value, ids);
+    expected.canonical_result = Some(snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&value));
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_result(value: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    match value {
+        Value::Id(id) => {
+            if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+                *id = replacement.clone();
+            }
+        }
+        Value::Array(values) => values.iter_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}

+writer/head fence. Before clearing targets, adoption derives each target's
+legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
+then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps. Thus an
+aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
+aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
+to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
+target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
+Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
+the same transaction. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
 `maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
 it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
 zero.

+For an insert or upsert that reuses an expired predecessor's id, insert
+authority is evaluated against the pre-retirement logical store. The engine

+uniqueness checks and physical insertion. At mutation commit, every row born
+or updated into an expired final image is retired through that same path. A
+refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
+earlier cascade and set-null writes.

+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match kind {
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}

   101	    /// Whether a read-through child remains outside a delete's cascade

   106	        parent: &str,

   108	        deleting: &BTreeSet<(String, String)>,

   280	            && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   281	        let patch = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, patch, readable)?;
   282	        let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &patch, readable)?;

   297	    fn upsert_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   298	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;

   308	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)

   310	            Some(old) => {

   435	    /// A delete's own removal of one row, its rules already decided: receipt

   437	    /// the partition event. A referential cascade removes each row this way.
   438	    pub(super) fn delete_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   439	        let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   440	        self.receipt_member_removed(table_name, &old)?;
   441	        self.refuse_live_children(table_name,old.field("id")?)?;
   442	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &old, Effect::Delete)?;
   443	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   444	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, &old)
   445	        })?;
   446	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), None, entries)?;
   447	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), None, Origin::Source)
   448	    }
   449	
   450	    /// Remove a row the engine itself retires (an expired one): no rule and
   451	    /// no constraint stands between the engine and its own sweep, while
   452	    /// aggregates and partition events apply as for any delete.
   453	    pub(super) fn remove(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   454	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   455	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   456	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   457	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, old)
   458	        })?;
   459	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(old), None, entries)?;
   460	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(old), None, Origin::Source)
   461	    }
   462	
   463	    /// Physically retire one row whose upper lifetime ended. Expiry bypasses
   464	    /// the root's authored delete rule and constraints, but it does not bypass
   465	    /// the schema's declared effects on rows that reference the root. A
   466	    /// read-through child still retains the expired parent physically.
   467	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — expiry cleanup runs the same closure/restrict/set-null actions as an authored delete.
   468	    pub(super) fn retire_expired_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   469	        if self.physical_children(table_name, old.field("id")?)? { return Ok(false); }
   470	        let current = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
   471	            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, old)?;
   472	            // A cascade may maintain a column on the root; delete its current
   473	            // physical image so index and cap entries match what is stored.
   474	            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?;
   475	            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))?
   476	                .unwrap_or_else(|| old.clone())
   477	        } else {
   478	            old.clone()
   479	        };
   480	        self.remove(table_name, &current)?;
   481	        Ok(true)
   482	    }
   483	
   484	    /// At a program commit's end, retire every source row the commit changed
   485	    /// or inserted whose lifetime has already ended: its final
   486	    /// image was never live at a commit boundary, so it leaves no row for a
   487	    /// later sweep to announce. Inside the commit the
   488	    /// row existed as written (an insert-then-update still works). Engine
   489	    /// bookkeeping, unmetered: the device's prediction does not do it, and
   490	    /// the program's metering is already recorded. Its work, returned, stays
   491	    /// linear in the rows retired: each aggregate row takes one net change
   492	    /// and each audience key is scanned for a live row once. Seeds and loads
   493	    /// keep their rows for the sweep.
   494	    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — a row whose lifetime ended by its own commit's end never exists at a commit boundary.
   495	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   496	    pub(crate) fn retire_expired_births(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
   497	        let Some(now) = self.context.now else { return Ok(Default::default());
   498	        };
   499	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#3 — an expired final image never grants a new recipient the row's id.
   500	        // The tracker covers synced and unsynced source tables alike. Each
   501	        // distinct entry prepaid its tree node, strings and this vector slot;
   502	        // the rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
   503	        // A row that existed before the commit and ends it already expired is
   504	        // retired too: accounted from the partitions it was in at the commit's
   505	        // start, it revokes there and announces nothing to a partition it only
   506	        // entered with its expiring image.
   507	        let mut changed: Vec<(String, String)> = std::mem::take(&mut self.expiry_rows).into_iter().collect();
   508	        if changed.is_empty() {
   509	            return Ok(Default::default());
   510	        }
   511	        // The log's order must not depend on a map's iteration order.
   512	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   513	        changed.sort_by_key(|(name,id)| {
   514	            (std::cmp::Reverse(order.iter().position(|n| n == name)),id.clone(),
   515	            )
   516	        });
   517	        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::meter::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort));
   518	        self.retiring = Some(Default::default());
   519	        let retired = changed.iter().try_for_each(|(table_name, id)| {
   520	            let Some(row) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))? else { return Ok(());
   521	            };
   522	            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   523	            if table.expired(&row, now) { self.retire_expired_row(table_name, &row).map(|_| ()) } else { Ok(()) }
   524	        });
   525	        let aggregates = self.retiring.take().map(|retiring| retiring.aggregates).unwrap_or_default();
   526	        let retired = retired.and_then(|()| self.apply_retired_aggregates(aggregates));
   527	        let work = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, meter).used;
   528	        retired.map(|()| work)
   529	    }
   530	
   531	    /// A column with a declared default takes it when the written row leaves
   532	    /// it out, before validation and before the asset facts, so the row the
   533	    /// rules and the constraints see is the complete one.
   534	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — omitted defaults use the clock and viewer of the host running the insert.
   535	    pub(super) fn with_defaults(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<Supplied, RuntimeError> {
   536	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   537	        if !table.defaults.keys().any(|name| {
   538	            row.as_object().is_ok_and(|fields| !fields.contains_key(name))
   539	        }) {
   540	            return Ok(row);
   541	        }
   542	        let row = row.defaults(table,self.context.now.ok_or_else(||RuntimeError::Input("write clock is not pinned".into()))?,&self.context.viewer)?;
   543	        self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?;
   544	        Ok(row)
   545	    }

   547	    /// An `image`/`video` column names an upload by id; the row carries the
   548	    /// facts the server established about it (type, bytes, dimensions,
   549	    /// duration), never the client's word for them. The upload must be the
   550	    /// writer's own and of the column's kind and size. The system principal
   551	    /// may name an asset that was never uploaded: a fixture's placeholder,
   552	    /// metadata only, never served.
   553	    // Web stores hold received asset facts, never the authoritative upload ledger.
   554	    #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
   555	    fn with_asset_facts(&mut self, _table_name: &str, row: Value, _old: Option<&Value>, _hidden_patch: Option<&Value>) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError> {
   556	        Ok(row)
   557	    }
   558	
   559	    pub(super) fn refuse_upsert_owned(&self, table: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   560	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table, Effect::Insert)?;
   561	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table, Effect::Update)
   562	    }
   563	
   564	    /// Programs never write a maintained target; the engine does.
   565	    pub(super) fn refuse_engine_owned(&self, table: &str, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   566	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — pending member changes cannot rewrite settled requirements.
   567	        if self.device && effect != Effect::Insert && self.schema.receipts.iter().any(|f| f.members == table || f.runs == table) {
   568	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("receipt membership changes and progress queue until settlement".into()));
   569	        }
   570	        self.refuse_receipt_table(table)?;
   571	        self.refuse_condition_write()?;
   572	        self.refuse_timeline_write(table, effect)?;
   573	        self.schema.refuse_private(table)?;
   574	        if self.schema.maintain_for(table).is_some() {
   575	            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table} is a maintained aggregate; write its source rows instead")));
   576	        }
   577	        Ok(())
   578	    }
   579	
   580	    fn check_constraints(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: &Value, effect: Effect) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   581	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   582	        let id = new.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   583	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#4.1 — an action's own write consults no rule: probing the child's read rule would draw the shared allowance only where a child exists.
   584	        let readable = match old { Some(old) if effect == Effect::Update && !self.engine_action => {
   585	                !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, old)?
   586	                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, old)?
   587	            }
   588	            _ => true };
   589	        if effect != Effect::Delete {
   590	            for (name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| index.unique) {
   591	                // byId can only return this id (already checked on insert).
   592	                // An unchanged admitted unique key cannot acquire a collision.
   593	                if name == "byId" { continue; }
   594	                let key = index_values(index, new);
   595	                if old.is_some_and(|old| index_values(index, old) == key) { continue; }
   596	                if key.iter().any(|value| *value == Value::Null) {
   597	                    continue;
   598	                }
   599	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — holding the target does not cover a different unique population.
   600	                if self.device && effect == Effect::Update && !self.device_work(|runner| {
   601	                        runner.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, name, &key)
   602	                    })? {
   603	                    return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, name, &key));
   604	                }
   605	                if let Some(existing) = self.collision_lookup(table_name, name, index, &key, Some(&id), effect)
   606	                    .map_err(|error| {
   607	                        if !readable && matches!(error, RuntimeError::Rule { .. }) { self.no_write_target() } else { error
   608	                        }
   609	                    })?
   610	                    && existing.field("id")?.as_str()? != id
   611	                {
   612	                    self.observe_sequence_columns(table_name, new, &index.columns(), effect == Effect::Insert)?;
   613	                    if effect == Effect::Update && !readable {
   614	                        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   615	                        self.refusing_clause(table_name, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")));
   616	                        return Err(self.no_write_target());
   617	                    }
   618	                    // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.9 — the dev log names the `unique` line that refused (wave 3 I3).
   619	                    self.refusing_clause(table_name, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")));
   620	                    let declared=index.components.iter().map(|part| match part {
   621	                        crate::schema::IndexComponent::Calendar(k) if k.function=="bucket" => format!("bucket({}, {}{})",k.column,k.millis,if k.offset==0 {String::new()} else {format!(", {}",k.offset)}),
   622	                        crate::schema::IndexComponent::Calendar(k)=>format!("{}({}{})",k.function,k.column,if k.offset==0 {String::new()} else {format!(", {}",k.offset)}),
   623	                        _=>part.key_name().cloned().unwrap_or_else(||"<key>".into()),
   624	                    }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
   625	                    let detail = format!("{table_name}: unique {declared} already has a row where {declared} = {}", key.iter().map(describe).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "));
   626	                    if let Some(refusal) = self.schema.unique_refusals.get(table_name).and_then(|indexes| indexes.get(name)) {
   627	                        return Err(RuntimeError::NamedConstraint { code: refusal.code.clone(), message: refusal.message.clone(), detail });
   628	                    }
   629	                    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#8 — the public code names uniqueness;
   630	                    // diagnostics use declared columns, never planner index names.
   631	                    return Err(RuntimeError::NamedConstraint { code: "E_UNIQUE".into(), message: detail.clone(), detail });
   632	                }
   633	            }
   634	        }
   635	        for constraint in &table.constraints {
   636	            match constraint {
   637	                Constraint::Capabilities(_) | Constraint::Recorded | Constraint::Unique { .. } | Constraint::Text { .. } | Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { .. } => {}
   638	                Constraint::AppendOnly => {
   639	                    if effect != Effect::Insert {
   640	                        return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("{table_name} is append-only")));
   641	                    }
   642	                }
   643	                Constraint::Immutable { fields } => {
   644	                    // Hidden patch fields were removed by ignore_hidden_immutable_patch;
   645	                    // do not turn this constraint into a second value comparison.
   646	                    if effect == Effect::Update && !readable { continue; }
   647	                    if let Some(old) = old
   648	                        && effect == Effect::Update
   649	                    {
   650	                        let mut old_image = old.clone();
   651	                        materialize_optional_fields(&mut old_image, table);
   652	                        let mut new_image = new.clone();
   653	                        materialize_optional_fields(&mut new_image, table);
   654	                        for field in fields {
   655	                            if old_image.field(field).ok() != new_image.field(field).ok() {
   656	                                if readable { self.refusing_clause(table_name, &format!("immutable {field}")); }
   657	                                return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("{table_name}.{field} is immutable")) } else { self.no_write_target() });
   658	                            }
   659	                        }
   660	                    }
   661	                }
   662	                Constraint::Cap { by, max } => {
   663	                    if effect == Effect::Delete {
   664	                        continue;
   665	                    }
   666	                    let group: Vec<Value> = by.iter().map(|field| new.field(field).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)).collect();
   667	                    // @ref LLP 3000.039#2.2 — a `set null` reference's null rows belong to no parent: its cap does not count them.
   668	                    if self.schema.cap_skips_null(table, by, &group) { continue; }
   669	                    // @ref LLP 3000.013#11.1 — an expired local predecessor may have been swept and its capacity refilled before sync arrives.
   670	                    let predecessor = old.filter(|row| !self.device || !self.expired(table, row));
   671	                    let moved = predecessor.is_none_or(|old| {
   672	                        by.iter().map(|field| old.field(field).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)).collect::<Vec<_>>() != group
   673	                    });
   674	                    if !moved {
   675	                        continue;
   676	                    }
   677	                    // A complete live snapshot omits unswept expired rows, so
   678	                    // its physical count cannot establish room on the server.
   679	                    // A count at the last delivered watermark would also be
   680	                    // stale after a sweep whose sync has not arrived yet.
   681	                    if self.device && table.is_expiring() {
   682	                        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("{table_name}'s expiring cap needs the server's physical occupancy; queue this write until the server settles it")));
   683	                    }
   684	                    let index_name = table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain() && index.columns().starts_with(by)).map(|(name, _)| name.clone()).ok_or_else(|| {
   685	                            RuntimeError::Schema(format!("cap by {} has no leading index", by.join(", ")))
   686	                        })?;
   687	                    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — moving a held row needs complete coverage of the destination cap group.
   688	                    if self.device && effect == Effect::Update && !self.device_work(|runner| {
   689	                            runner.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, &index_name, &group)
   690	                        })? {
   691	                        return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, &index_name, &group));
   692	                    }
   693	                    let private_cap = !table.sequences.is_empty() && !self.context.is_system() && !table.rules.read.is_uniformly_readable();
   694	                    let count = self.authorized_scan(&[
   695	                        (MeterKind::IndexEntries, 1),
   696	                        (MeterKind::Examined, if private_cap { *max as u64 } else { 0 },
   697	                            ),
   698	                        (MeterKind::RuleProbes, if private_cap { super::rules::rule_probes(&table.rules.read).saturating_mul(*max as u64) } else { 0 },
   699	                            ),
   700	                    ], |runner, allowance| {
   701	                        if !private_cap && !table.is_expiring() {
   702	                            return runner.tx.count_prefix(allowance, table_name, &index_name, &group, *max as u64 + 1);
   703	                        }
   704	                        // Main's transactional occupancy is a cheap upper bound
   705	                        // on live rows. Below the cap it proves room without a
   706	                        // walk; at the cap, B2's bounded live scan decides. A
   707	                        // private sequence cap must still authorize occupants.
   708	                        if !private_cap {
   709	                            let physical = runner.tx.cap_count(allowance, table_name, by, &group)?;
   710	                            if physical < *max as u64 { return Ok(physical); }
   711	                        }
   712	                        let mut count = 0;
   713	                        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   714	                        loop {
   715	                            // Expired occupants consume physical work, never
   716	                            // hidden-dependent logical charges. Exhaustion
   717	                            // cannot establish occupancy and reveals no detail.
   718	                            let batch = runner.tx.remaining().min(32);
   719	                            if batch == 0 { return Err(RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget { table: table_name.into(), effect }); }
   720	                            let rows = runner.tx.scan(allowance, table_name, &index_name, &group, &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)?;
   721	                            let fetched = rows.len();
   722	                            for (row, key) in rows {
   723	                                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key).map(|values| {
   724	                                        values.into_iter().skip(group.len()).collect()
   725	                                    });
   726	                                if !runner.expired(table, &row) {
   727	                                    if private_cap { runner.visible_collision(table_name, &row, effect, &format!("cap {}", by.join(", ")))?; }
   728	                                    count += 1;
   729	                                }
   730	                                if count >= *max as u64 { break; }
   731	                            }
   732	                            if count >= *max as u64 || fetched < batch { break; }
   733	                        }
   734	                        Ok(count)
   735	                    })?;
   736	                    if count >= *max as u64 {
   737	                        self.observe_sequence_columns(table_name, new, by, effect == Effect::Insert)?;
   738	                        // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — cap diagnostics describe the schema, never retained group values.
   739	                        // @ref LLP 3000.040#32-changes — a whole-table cap has no group to name.
   740	                        let (clause, message) = if by.is_empty() {
   741	                            (format!("cap {max}"), format!("{table_name} holds at most {max} rows"),
   742	                            )
   743	                        } else {
   744	                            (format!("cap {}", by.join(", ")), format!("{table_name} holds at most {max} rows per group by {}", by.join(", ")),
   745	                            )
   746	                        };
   747	                        self.refusing_clause(table_name, &clause);
   748	                        return Err(if table.is_expiring() {
   749	                            RuntimeError::ExpiringCap { message, site: self.statement_site.clone() }
   750	                        } else { RuntimeError::Constraint(message) });
   751	                    }
   752	                }
   753	            }
   754	        }
   755	        Ok(())
   756	    }
   757	
   758	    fn collision_lookup(&mut self, table: &str, name: &str, index: &crate::schema::Index, key: &[Value], except: Option<&str>, effect: Effect) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
   759	        let probes = super::rules::rule_probes(&self.schema.tables[table].rules.read);
   760	        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes)], |runner, allowance| {
   761	            let found = if runner.schema.tables[table].not_before.is_some() {
   762	                runner.lookup_write_occupant(table, name, index, key)?
   763	            } else {
   764	                runner.live_lookup(allowance, table, name, index, key, #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] None)?
   765	            };
   766	            if let Some(row) = &found && Some(row.field("id")?.as_str()?) != except {
   767	                runner.observe_sequence_columns(table, row, &index.columns(), effect == Effect::Insert)?;
   768	                runner.visible_collision(table, row, effect, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")))?;
   769	            }
   770	            Ok(found)
   771	        })
   772	    }
   773	
   774	    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — hidden collisions use the ordinary write-rule refusal
   775	    fn visible_collision(
   776	        &mut self,
   777	        table: &str,
   778	        row: &Value,
   779	        effect: Effect,
   780	        clause: &str,
   781	    ) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   782	        let mut image = row.clone();
   783	        let definition = self.schema.table(table).expect("validated");
   784	        materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, definition);
   785	        if self.inactive_write_target(table, &image)? || !self.check_rule(table, Effect::Read, None, &image)? {
   786	            return Err(self.rule_refusal(table, effect, clause));
   787	        }
   788	        Ok(())
   789	    }
   790	
   791	    /// `after insert <- exists t[...]` holds for every row inserted this
   792	    /// transaction; checked once the program has run.
   793	    pub(super) fn check_final_exists(&mut self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   794	        let inserted = std::mem::take(&mut self.inserted);
   795	        for (table_name, row) in &inserted {
   796	            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   797	            for constraint in &table.constraints {
   798	                let Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key } = constraint else { continue;
   799	                };
   800	                let refusal = || {
   575	        let programs = programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)).collect();
   576	        drop(self.ephemeral.lock()?);
   577	        let (generation, metadata) = Self::activate(&mut self.store, &schema, &programs, None, now, true, None, None)?;
   578	        self.timeline_schedule = timeline::Schedule::default();
   579	        self.schema = schema;
   580	        self.programs = programs;
   581	        self.generation = generation;
   582	        self.expiry_after.clear();
   583	        self.ephemeral.rebind_committed(metadata.store_id, generation, &self.schema);
   584	        Ok(generation)
   585	    }
   586	
   587	
   588	    /// Delete the rows past their `expire` column. They were absent to
   589	    /// every reader from the moment they expired; the sweep makes that
   590	    /// physical, so the log carries the deletion to each device holding
   591	    /// them. At most `limit` rows go in one commit; the next pass continues.
   592	    pub fn sweep_expired(&mut self, now: i64, limit: usize) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   593	        self.sweep_expired_for(now, limit, std::time::Duration::MAX)
   594	    }
   595	
   596	    /// Stop between row removals; a short sweep can still leave due rows.
   597	    pub fn sweep_expired_for(&mut self, now: i64, limit: usize, budget: std::time::Duration) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   598	        // Expiry cleanup is recovery work. Pin the same authoritative clock,
   599	        // but commit physical cleanup before attempting a due opening so a
   600	        // refused publication can never wedge the rows whose upper lifetime
   601	        // has already ended.
   602	        let now = self.pin_time_audience(now)?;
   603	        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
   604	        let expiring: Vec<(String, String)> = self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().filter(|name| self.schema.tables[name].ephemeral.is_none()).filter_map(|name| {

    13	/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
    14	/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an
    15	/// earlier table contains a permanently restricted due row.
    16	pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(
    17	    mut tables: Vec<String>,
    18	    cursors: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>,
    19	) -> Vec<String> {
    20	    let after = cursors
    21	        .get(EXPIRY_TABLE_CURSOR)
    22	        .and_then(|cursor| cursor.first())
    23	        .and_then(|value| value.as_str().ok());
    24	    if let Some(index) = after.and_then(|after| tables.iter().position(|table| table == after)) {
    25	        let next = (index + 1) % tables.len().max(1);
    26	        tables.rotate_left(next);
    27	    }
    28	    tables
    29	}

   113	    if child.is_uniformly_readable() && parent.is_uniformly_readable() {
   114	        return Some(Default::default());
   115	    }
   116	    fn walk(
   117	        a: &serde_json::Value,
   118	        b: &serde_json::Value,
   119	        map: &mut std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,
   120	    ) -> bool {
   121	        use serde_json::Value::*;
   122	        match (a, b) {
   123	            (Object(a), Object(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
   124	                if let (Some(String(a)), Some(String(b))) = (a.get("Field"), b.get("Field")) {
   125	                    if map.get(a).is_some_and(|old| old != b)
   126	                        || map.iter().any(|(old, v)| v == b && old != a)
   127	                    {
   128	                        return false;
   129	                    }
   130	                    map.insert(a.clone(), b.clone());
   131	                    true
   132	                } else {
   133	                    a.iter()
   134	                        .all(|(k, a)| b.get(k).is_some_and(|b| walk(a, b, map)))
   135	                }
   136	            }
   137	            (Array(a), Array(b)) if a.len() == b.len() => {
   138	                a.iter().zip(b).all(|(a, b)| walk(a, b, map))
   139	            }
   140	            _ => a == b,
   141	        }
   142	    }
   143	    let mut map = Default::default();
   144	    walk(
   145	        &serde_json::to_value(child).ok()?,
   146	        &serde_json::to_value(parent).ok()?,
   147	        &mut map,
   148	    )
   149	    .then_some(map)
   150	}

   382	pub fn validate_indexes(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   383	    for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
   384	        let mut checks: Vec<_> = table
   385	            .indexes
   386	            .iter()
   387	            .filter(|(_, i)| i.unique)
   388	            .map(|(name, i)| (name, i.components.len(), 1, true))
   389	            .collect();
   390	        for constraint in &table.constraints {
   391	            if let crate::schema::Constraint::Cap { by, max } = constraint {
   392	                let (index, _) = table
   393	                    .indexes
   394	                    .iter()
   395	                    .find(|(_, i)| i.columns().starts_with(by))
   396	                    .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{name} cap has no index")))?;
   397	                checks.push((index, by.len(), u64::from(*max), false));
   398	            }
   399	        }
   400	        for (index, width, max, nulls_distinct) in checks {
   401	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   402	            let mut previous = None;
   403	            let mut count = 0;
   404	            loop {
   405	                let page = tx.scan(name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
   406	                if page.is_empty() {
   407	                    break;
   408	                }
   409	                for (_, key) in page {
   410	                    let full = crate::key::decode(&key)
   411	                        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("invalid activation index".into()))?;
   412	                    let group = full[..width].to_vec();
   413	                    bounds.after = Some(full);
   414	                    if nulls_distinct && group.contains(&Value::Null) {
   415	                        continue;
   416	                    }
   417	                    if previous.as_ref() == Some(&group) {
   418	                        count += 1;
   419	                    } else {
   420	                        previous = Some(group);
   421	                        count = 1;
   422	                    }
   423	                    if count > max {
   424	                        return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!(
   425	                            "cannot activate {name}.{index}: existing group exceeds {max}"
   426	                        )));
   427	                    }
   428	                }
   429	            }
   430	        }
   431	    }
   432	    Ok(())
   433	}

   438	    pub fn seed_server_rows(
   439	        &mut self,
   440	        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
   441	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   442	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {

   444	                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
   445	            ));
   446	        }
   447	        let order = self.schema.through_order();

   449	        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
   450	        let count = rows.len() as u64;
   451	        for (name, row) in rows {
   452	            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
   453	            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
   454	            self.upsert(
   455	                &name,
   456	                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
   457	                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
   458	            )?;
   459	        }

   461	        Ok(count)
   462	    }

   464	    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
   465	    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   466	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   467	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   468	                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
   469	            ));
   470	        }
   471	        let now = self
   472	            .context
   473	            .now
   474	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   475	        let mut count = 0;
   476	        let mut visited = 0;
   477	        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
   478	        for name in tables {
   479	            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
   480	                continue;
   481	            };
   482	            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   483	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   484	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
   485	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   486	            while visited < limit {
   487	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   488	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
   489	                    runner
   490	                        .tx
   491	                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
   492	                })?;
   493	                if page.is_empty() {
   494	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   495	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   496	                        bounds = due.clone();
   497	                        wrapped = true;
   498	                        continue;
   499	                    }
   500	                    break;
   501	                }
   502	                let page_len = page.len();
   503	                for (row, key) in page {
   504	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   505	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   506	                    visited += 1;
   507	                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
   508	                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
   509	                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
   510	                        Ok(false) => {},
   511	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
   512	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   513	                    }
   514	                }
   515	                if page_len < batch {
   516	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   517	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   518	                        bounds = due.clone();
   519	                        wrapped = true;
   520	                        continue;
   521	                    }
   522	                    break;
   523	                }
   524	            }
   525	        }
   526	        Ok(count)
   527	    }
   528	}
     1	//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
     2	//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
     3	//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
     4	use super::*;
     5	
     6	pub(super) fn install(
     7	    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
     8	    schema: &Schema,
     9	    creating: bool,
    10	    generation: u64,
    11	) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    12	    let current = tx.query(
    13	        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
    14	        &[],
    15	    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
    16	    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
    17	        return Ok(generation);
    18	    }
    19	
    20	    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
    21	        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
    22	        .cloned()
    23	        .collect();
    24	    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
    25	        let mut runner = Runner::new(
    26	            tx,
    27	            schema,
    28	            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
    29	            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
    30	            tx.next_seq()?,
    31	        );
    32	        runner.event_free = true;
    33	        runner.rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&aggregates)?;
    34	        for maintain in &aggregates {
    35	            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
    36	        }
    37	    }
    38	
    39	    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
    40	        generation
    41	    } else {
    42	        generation.checked_add(1)
    43	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
    44	    };
    45	    tx.execute(
    46	        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
    47	        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
    48	    )?;
    49	    Ok(generation)
    50	}

    47	        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
    48	        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
    49	            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
    50	        _ => false,
    51	    }
    52	}
