    55	    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — no predicted delta enters receipt-derived state.
    56	    pub(super) fn defer_receipt_maintain(&self, m: &Maintain) -> bool {
    57	        self.device && self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target)
    58	    }
    59	
    60	    // Cache ordinary group keys once per target/query. Predicates and receipt
    61	    // fields are never evaluated; unknown/computed keys conservatively freeze
    62	    // the target. An unpinned read is incomplete if any group is dirty, while
    63	    // each returned row still decides independently whether to recount.
    64	    #[inline(never)]
    65	    pub(super) fn receipt_maintain_pending(&mut self, m: &Maintain, group: Option<&[Value]>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    66	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(false); }
    67	        if !self.receipt_pending_groups.contains_key(&m.target) {
    68	            let fields = if let Some(k) = &m.row_key { vec![k.source_key.clone()] }
    69	                else { m.by.iter().map(|f| m.aliases.get(f).unwrap_or(f).clone()).collect() };
    70	            let mut groups = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&m.source, &fields, !m.computed.is_empty())?;
    71	            if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
    72	                let member = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&k.table, std::slice::from_ref(&k.member_key), false)?;
    73	                groups = groups.zip(member).map(|(mut source, member)| { source.extend(member); source });
    74	            }
    75	            self.receipt_pending_groups.insert(m.target.clone(), groups);
    76	        }
    77	        let dirty = self.receipt_pending_groups[&m.target].as_ref().is_none_or(|keys|
    78	            group.map_or(!keys.is_empty(), |group| keys.iter().any(|key| key == group)));
    79	        if dirty {
    80	            self.value_source_incomplete = true;
    81	            self.components.note(|frame| frame.pending = true);
    82	        }
    83	        Ok(dirty)
    84	    }
    85	
    86	    fn receipt_overlay_groups(&self, table: &str, fields: &[String], computed: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<Vec<Value>>>, RuntimeError> {
    87	        if !self.tx.has_provisional(table)? { return Ok(Some(Vec::new())); }
    88	        if computed || fields.iter().any(|f| self.schema.receipt_dependencies.get(table).is_some_and(|owned| owned.contains(f))) {
    89	            return Ok(None);
    90	        }
    91	        self.tx.provisional_groups(table, fields)
    92	    }
    93	
    94	    // Recover a read's parent/group from the pinned index. A member point uses
    95	    // one ordinary-key lookup; a scan without the parent stays conservative.
    96	    pub(super) fn receipt_read_group(&mut self, m: &Maintain, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Vec<Value>>, RuntimeError> {
    97	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(None); }
    98	        let columns = self.schema.tables[&m.target].indexes[index].columns();
    99	        let pinned = |field: &str| columns.iter().position(|c| c == field).and_then(|i| key.get(i)).cloned();
   100	        if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
   101	            if let Some(parent) = pinned(&k.member_key) { return Ok(Some(vec![parent])); }
   102	            if let Some(id) = pinned("member").or_else(|| pinned("id")) {
   103	                let row = self.metered_scan(|r, scope| r.tx.get(scope, &k.table, id.as_str()?))?;
   104	                return Ok(row.and_then(|row| row.field(&k.member_key).ok().cloned()).map(|v| vec![v]));
   105	            }
   106	            return Ok(None);
   107	        }
   108	        Ok(m.by.iter().map(|f| pinned(f)).collect())
   109	    }

   111	    pub(super) fn maintain(&mut self, source: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   112	        self.receipt_pending_groups.clear();
   113	        // Inserts ordinarily charge their actual aggregate work. A deferred
   114	        // predicate cannot select that work on a device, so use the same public
   115	        // worst-case reservation as update/delete before skipping it. Already
   116	        // prepaid writes must not pay twice.
   117	        if self.device && !self.maintain_prepaid && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|
   118	            m.source == source && m.private.is_none() && m.row_key.is_none() && (self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target) || self.schema.tables[&m.target].sync.is_none())) {
   119	            self.reserve_maintains(source, &self.schema.tables[source])?;
   120	        }
   121	        self.maintain_row_views(source, old, new)?;
   122	        let maintains = self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.source == source && maintain.row_key.is_none());
   123	        for maintain in maintains {
   124	            if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) || (self.device && self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].sync.is_none()) { continue; }
   125	            let source_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]);
   126	            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
   127	            let bytes = source_bytes.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64));
   128	            let prepaid = self.maintain_prepaid;
   129	            if maintain.private.is_some() && self.column_prepaid { self.maintain_prepaid = true; }
   130	            let result = self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.maintain_one(maintain, old, new));
   131	            self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
   132	            result?;
   133	        }
   134	        Ok(())
   135	    }
   136	
   137	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
   138	    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   139	        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
   140	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
   141	        let result = work(self);
   142	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
   143	        result
   144	    }

   146	    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   147	        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   148	        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
   149	        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
   150	            let Some(image) = image else { continue };
   151	            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
   152	            let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, table);
   153	            if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
   154	            let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
   155	            let change = delta(maintain, &image, direction)?;
   156	            if let Some(existing) = changes.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == key) { existing.1 += change; }
   157	            else { changes.push((key, change)); }
   158	        }
   159	        for (key, change) in changes {
   160	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   161	            if let Some(retiring) = self.retiring.as_mut() {
   162	                let entry = retiring.aggregates.entry((maintain.target.clone(), canonical_json(&key))).or_insert_with(|| (key, 0));
   163	                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
   164	                continue;
   165	            }
   166	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   167	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   168	            }
   169	        }
   170	        Ok(())
   171	    }
   172	
   173	    /// Apply a retirement's net aggregate changes, one per target row, in
   174	    /// key order. Only a total the commit really ends with can overflow.
   175	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   176	    pub(super) fn apply_retired_aggregates(&mut self, changes: BTreeMap<(String, String), (Vec<Value>, i128)>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   177	        let schema = self.schema;
   178	        for ((target, _), (key, change)) in changes {
   179	            let maintain = schema.maintain_for(&target).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing maintain for {target}")))?;
   180	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   181	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
   182	            }
   183	        }
   184	        Ok(())
   185	    }

   197	    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then

   200	    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
   201	    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
   202	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   203	    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain]) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   204	        let mut legacy = Vec::new();
   205	        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {

   212	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   213	            loop {
   214	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   215	                if page.is_empty() { break; }

   217	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   218	                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   219	                    let key = fields.iter().map(|(field, kind)| Ok((kind.clone(), row.field(field)?.clone())))
   220	                        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?;

   223	            }
   224	            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));

   230	        // than target tables: one aggregate target may contain an arbitrary
   231	        // acyclic chain of references to other rows in that same target.
   232	        let identity_count = legacy.iter().map(|(_, rows)| rows.len()).sum::<usize>();

   234	        // additional observation pass even when every target is empty.

   253	            }

   368	    fn live_sum(&self, maintain: &Maintain) -> bool {

   405	    fn apply_aggregate(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: Vec<Value>, change: i128, source_present: Option<bool>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

    56	impl PostgresEngine {
    57	    /// Create a NEW, isolated sb4_eval_* namespace; never replace an existing
    58	    /// schema. TLS/credentials are owned by the caller's configured Client.
    59	    pub fn create(
    60	        client: Client,
    61	        name: &str,
    62	        mut schema: Schema,
    63	        programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
    64	    ) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
    65	        let name = namespace(name)?;
    66	        refuse_maintained_columns(&schema)?;
    67	        super::columns::validate_before_prepare(&schema)?;
    68	        schema.prepare_contribution_indexes();
    69	        let programs: BTreeMap<_, _> = programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)).collect();
    70	        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
    71	        Self::attach(client, schema, programs, Some(&name))
    72	    }
    73	
    74	    /// Reopen the persisted compiled generation; subsequent transactions refuse
    75	    /// if another connection activates a successor.
    76	    pub fn open(mut client: Client, name: &str) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
    77	        let name = namespace(name)?;
    78	        client.batch_execute(&format!("SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
    79	        let row = client.query_one("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;
    80	        if row.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
    81	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
    82	        }
    83	        let schema = decode(row.get(1))?;
    84	        let programs = decode(row.get(2))?;
    85	        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
    86	        // Existing immutable stores adopt this portable admission policy at open.
    87	        // Return one offending index and its exact count, never its row payloads.
    88	        if let Some(row) = client.query(
    89	            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
    90	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
    91	        )?.first() {
    92	            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
    93	        }
    94	        Self::attach(client, schema, programs, None)
    95	    }

    97	    // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.3 — read-session storage and all other upgrades
    98	    // commit together, only after every open/adoption check has succeeded.
    99	    fn attach(client: Client, mut schema: Schema, programs: BTreeMap<String, Program>, create: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
   100	        let mut store = Store::new(client);
   101	        let tx = store.opening_transaction()?;
   102	        tx.batch("SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s'; SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';")?;

   107	                &[&store::VERSION, &canonical_json(&schema), &canonical_json(&programs)])?;
   108	        }
   109	        tx.query("SELECT seq FROM _head WHERE singleton FOR UPDATE", &[])?;
   110	        // Admission must use the backend that survived the wait for the head.
   111	        // A format change can leave schema/program bytes unchanged.
   112	        let held = tx.query("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?.remove(0);
   113	        if held.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
   114	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
   115	        }
   116	        let held_schema: Schema = decode(held.get(1))?;
   117	        let held_programs: BTreeMap<String, Program> = decode(held.get(2))?;
   118	        supported(&held_schema, &held_programs)?;
   119	        if held_schema.hash() != schema.hash() || canonical_json(&held_programs) != canonical_json(&programs) {
   120	            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the backend changed while opening; reopen its current generation".into()));
   121	        }
   122	        // Even a no-op ALTER takes an exclusive table lock. Reopening an
   123	        // upgraded store must remain possible while another reader holds it.
   124	        for (column, ddl) in [
   125	            ("generation", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
   126	            ("through_shortened", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN through_shortened TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'"),
   127	            ("maintained_identity_version", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN maintained_identity_version TEXT"),
   128	        ] {

   138	        }

   151	    }

   183	    pub fn query_with_delivery(&mut self, name: &str, mut context: Context, manifest: super::DeliveryManifest) -> Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal> {
   184	        context.generation = self.generation();
   185	        let program = self.programs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::UnknownOp(name.into()))?;
   186	        if program.kind != ProgramKind::Query {
   187	            return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp(format!("{name} is not a query")).into());
   188	        }
   189	        super::server_query_allowed(&self.schema, name)?;
   190	        validate::validate_inputs(&self.schema, program, &mut context.args)?;
   191	        context.now.get_or_insert_with(crate::now_ms);
   192	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
   193	        let seq = tx.next_seq()? - 1;
   194	        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, context, Meter::new(self.ceilings, Cut::Cap), seq);
   195	        runner.meter.used = self.precharge;
   196	        let data = runner.run(program)?;
   197	        runner.charge_output(&data)?;

     7	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]

     9	pub enum OnDelete {
    10	    Restrict,
    11	    Cascade,
    12	    SetNull,
    13	    /// The referencing row stays and names a deleted row (the pre-0.5 meaning),
    14	    /// declared on purpose: history, audit trails, contributions that outlive
    15	    /// their target.
    16	    Keep,
    17	}

    19	impl OnDelete {
    20	    pub fn words(self) -> &'static str {
    21	        match self { Self::Restrict => "on delete restrict", Self::Cascade => "on delete cascade", Self::SetNull => "on delete set null", Self::Keep => "on delete keep" }
    22	    }
    23	    /// The actions that write the children, bounded by a cap on the reference.
    24	    pub fn writes(self) -> bool { matches!(self, Self::Cascade | Self::SetNull) }
    25	    /// The actions a delete must consult (every one but `keep`).
    26	    pub fn acts(self) -> bool { self != Self::Keep }
    27	}
    28	
    29	/// One action-carrying reference `child.column -> parent`.
    30	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
    31	pub struct Referencing<'a> {
    32	    pub child: &'a str,
    33	    pub table: &'a Table,
    34	    pub column: &'a str,
    35	    pub action: OnDelete,
    36	}
    37	
    38	/// The prefix of the reference index a live child of `parent` is found under.
    39	pub const REFERENCE_INDEX_PREFIX: &str = "$reference:";
    40	pub fn reference_index_name(column: &str) -> String { format!("{REFERENCE_INDEX_PREFIX}{column}") }
    41	
    42	/// Heap a closure keeps per reached row: its table and id (an id is at most
    43	/// 144 canonical bytes) and the set and queue entries holding them.
    44	pub const CLOSURE_IDENTITY_BYTES: u64 = 384;
    45	/// Child rows a cascade or set-null walk reads per seek (LLP 3000.039 §5.1).
    46	pub const REFERENCE_PAGE: usize = 4;

    50	    /// parent: an ordinary durable application table. Ephemeral rows, engine
    51	    /// derivations and receipt/timeline bookkeeping keep their own lifetimes.
    52	    pub fn actionable(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
    53	        let Some(table) = self.table(name) else { return false };
    54	        table.ephemeral.is_none() && self.maintain_for(name).is_none() && self.private_owner(name).is_none()

    56	            && !self.receipts.iter().any(|f| [&f.scope, &f.members, &f.runs].iter().any(|t| t.as_str() == name))

    59	    /// Every reference into `parent` a delete consults (all but `keep`), in
    60	    /// (child, column) order.
    61	    pub fn referencing<'a>(&'a self, parent: &str) -> Vec<Referencing<'a>> {
    62	        // A plain loop into a vector: iterator adapters monomorphize per call site on the web device.
    63	        let mut out = Vec::new();
    64	        for (child, table) in &self.tables {
    65	            for (column, action) in &table.on_delete {
    66	                if action.acts() && matches!(table.columns.get(column).map(ColumnType::required), Some(ColumnType::Ref { table: target }) if target == parent) {
    67	                    out.push(Referencing { child, table, column, action: *action });
    68	                }
    69	            }
    70	        }
    71	        out
    72	    }

    74	    /// A delete of a `parent` row consults its referencing rows, so it needs

    76	    pub fn is_referenced(&self, parent: &str) -> bool { !self.referencing(parent).is_empty() }

    81	    pub fn reference_index(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<&str> {

     1	import Quarry.Eval
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Writes: rule checks and refusals
     5	
     6	From the rules card, `why E_RULE`, `why NOT_FOUND`, `why E_CONFLICT` and the
     7	writes card:
     8	
     9	* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on
    10	  `id` or a declared unique key with a hidden row is `E_RULE`; with a visible
    11	  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`
    12	  or the key's `else CODE`.
    13	* **update** — "readable" means the read rule admits the old row before the
    14	  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
    15	  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is
    16	  `NOT_FOUND`; an `if` condition on an unreadable target is `NOT_FOUND`, and a
    17	  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is
    18	  `NOT_FOUND` (unreadable target), `E_RULE` (hidden colliding row) or
    19	  `E_CONSTRAINT`. An admitted update may change a hidden row; the result is
    20	  the row if it is readable afterwards, else null.
    21	* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent
    22	  one, where an incomplete image or insert-rule denial is `NOT_FOUND`.
    23	* **delete** — `NOT_FOUND` for a missing or unreadable refused target,
    24	  `E_RULE` for a readable one whose delete rule refuses. A row that
    25	  `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` references name also needs read
    26	  authority (`NOT_FOUND`); then its delete closes over `cascade` references,
    27	  refuses `E_REFERENCED` while a `restrict` reference names a closure row
    28	  from outside the closure, clears `set null` references outside it, and
    29	  removes the closure (LLP 3000.039 §3).
    30	
    31	The order in which checks run when several fail is not documented; the
    32	model's order is OPEN W1–W6.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	namespace Quarry
    36	
    37	def notFound : Stop := .refuse "NOT_FOUND"
    38	def eRule : Stop := .refuse "E_RULE"
    39	def eInput : Stop := .refuse "E_INPUT"
    40	
    41	def toScalarE : Value → Except Stop Scalar
    42	  | .s x => pure x
    43	  | _ => throw eInput
    44	
    45	def scalarsE (fs : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop (List (String × Scalar)) :=
    46	  fs.mapM fun p => do return (p.1, ← toScalarE p.2)
    47	
    48	/-- A column value fits its declaration: only a nullable column takes null. -/
    49	def fits (c : ColDecl) (x : Scalar) : Bool := c.nullable || x != .null
    50	
    51	/-- The new image of an insert. An absent nullable column is null; an absent
    52	required column refuses with `missing`. Unknown fields refuse `E_INPUT`. -/
    53	def buildImage (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) (fields : List (String × Scalar))
    54	    (missing : Stop) : Except Stop Row := do
    55	  if fields.any fun p => p.1 != "id" && !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
    56	  let cols ← td.cols.mapM fun c => match fields.lookup c.name with
    57	    | some x => if fits c x then pure (c.name, x) else throw eInput
    58	    | none => if c.nullable then pure (c.name, Scalar.null) else throw missing
    59	  return { id := rid, cols }
    60	
    61	/-- The next image of an update: the patch replaces named columns. -/
    62	def patchImage (td : TableDecl) (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop Row := do
    63	  if patch.any fun p => !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
    64	  let cols ← old.cols.mapM fun p => match patch.lookup p.1 with
    65	    | some x =>
    66	      match td.cols.find? (·.name == p.1) with
    67	      | some c => if fits c x then pure (p.1, x) else throw eInput
    68	      | none => throw eInput
    69	    | none => pure p
    70	  return { old with cols }
    71	
    72	def keyOf (cols : List String) (r : Row) : List (String × Scalar) := cols.map fun c => (c, r.get c)
    73	
    74	/-- The first unique key (in order) on which another row (not `except`)
    75	collides with `img`. Keys with a null component never collide (a nullable
    76	unique key permits tied nulls; indexes card). -/
    77	def findClash (rows : List Row) (keys : List (List String)) (img : Row) (except : Option (List Nat)) :
    78	    Option (Nat × Row) :=
    79	  let rec go (i : Nat) : List (List String) → Option (Nat × Row)
    80	    | [] => none
    81	    | k :: ks =>
    82	      let kv := keyOf k img
    83	      if kv.any (·.2 == .null) then go (i + 1) ks
    84	      else match rows.find? (fun r => keyMatch kv r && except != some r.id) with
    85	        | some r => some (i, r)
    86	        | none => go (i + 1) ks
    87	  go 0 keys
    88	
    89	/-- The refusal for a visible clash on unique key `i` of `["id"] ++ uniques`
    90	(`withId`) or of `uniques`. -/
    91	def clashCode (td : TableDecl) (withId : Bool) (i : Nat) : Stop :=
    92	  let j := if withId then i - 1 else i
    93	  if withId && i = 0 then .refuse "E_CONSTRAINT"
    94	  else match td.uniqueCodes[j]? with
    95	    | some (some code) => .refuse code
    96	    | _ => .refuse "E_UNIQUE"
    97	
    98	def findRow (rows : List Row) (ks : List (String × Scalar)) : Option Row :=
    99	  if ks.any (·.2 == .null) then none else rows.find? (keyMatch ks)
   100

   102	/-- A write target lookup selects among live rows, rather than selecting a
   103	physical predecessor and rejecting it after it has hidden a live match. -/
   104	def findLiveRow (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (rows : List Row)
   105	    (ks : List (String × Scalar)) : Option Row :=
   106	  findRow (rows.filter (unexpired td now)) ks
   107	
   108	/-- The result of a write: the row if the viewer can read it afterwards,
   109	else null (`why E_CONFLICT`: results are read-rule gets; OPEN W4 for insert). -/
   110	def resultOf (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
   111	  if readable sch s v t r then r.toValue else .null
   112	
   113	def resultOfAt (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
   114	    (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
   115	  if readableAt sch s v now t r then r.toValue else .null
   116	
   117	/-- `guardE b e` continues when `b` holds and refuses `e` otherwise. -/
   118	def guardE (b : Bool) (e : Stop) : Except Stop Unit := if b then .ok () else .error e
   119	
   120	def doInsertImage (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   121	    (img : Row) (clashHidden : Stop) :
   122	    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do
   123	  -- Insert authority has already been checked. Remaining unique checks and
   124	  -- the physical insertion use the post-retirement store.
   125	  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none with
   126	  | some (i, r) => do
   127	    guardE (readableAt sch s v now t r) clashHidden

   129	  | none =>

   131	    pure (resultOfAt sch s' v now t img, s')
   132	
   133	/-- An update's `if` condition: `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable target,
   134	`E_CONFLICT` when false. -/
   135	def condCheck (rd : Bool) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) (old : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
   136	  match cond with
   137	  | some f => do
   138	    guardE rd notFound
   139	    let b ← f old
   140	    guardE b (.refuse "E_CONFLICT")
   141	  | none => pure ()
   142	
   143	/-- A secondary unique clash of an update's next image with another row. -/
   144	def clashCheck (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   145	    (rd : Bool) (old nw : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
   146	  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) td.uniques nw (some old.id) with
   147	  | some (i, r) =>
   148	    throw (if !rd then notFound else if !(readableAt sch s v now t r) then eRule else clashCode td false i)
   149	  | none => pure ()
   150	
   151	def doUpdateRow (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   152	    (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) :
   153	    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do
   154	  let nw ← patchImage td old patch
   155	  guardE (td.update.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { old := some old, next := some nw })

   159	  pure (resultOfAt sch (s.replaceRow t old nw) v now t nw, s.replaceRow t old nw)

   162	def upsertId (ks ps : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop (List Nat) :=

   174	/-! ## Referential actions (LLP 3000.039 §3) -/
   175	
   176	/-- Every reference that names table `t` and carries an action:
   177	`(child table, column, action)`. -/
   178	def referencing (sch : Schema) (t : String) : List (String × String × OnDelete) :=
   179	  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => td.cols.filterMap fun c =>
   180	    match c.ref, c.onDelete with
   181	    | some p, some a => if p == t then some (td.name, c.name, a) else none
   182	    | _, _ => none
   183	
   184	/-- Row `k` names the row with id `i` through column `c`. -/
   185	def names (k : Row) (c : String) (i : List Nat) : Bool := k.get c == .id i
   186	
   187	def inClosure (cl : List (String × Row)) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   188	  cl.any fun p => p.1 == t && p.2.id == r.id
   189	
   190	/-- The rows one step of cascades reaches from `(t, r)`. -/
   191	def cascadeKids (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : List (String × Row) :=
   192	  (referencing sch t).flatMap fun (c, col, a) =>
   193	    if a == .cascade then ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id).map fun k => (c, k) else []
   194	
   195	/-- Breadth-first closure over `cascade` references, each row once; `fuel`
   196	bounds the walk (the store's row count suffices). -/
   197	def closure (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row)
   198	  | 0, _, acc => acc
   199	  | _ + 1, [], acc => acc
   200	  | f + 1, (t, r) :: rest, acc =>
   201	    let new := (cascadeKids sch s t r).foldl (fun n p => if inClosure (acc ++ n) p.1 p.2 then n else n ++ [p]) []
   202	    closure sch s f (rest ++ new) (acc ++ new)
   203	
   204	/-- Some `restrict` reference names a closure row from outside the closure. -/
   205	def restricted (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (cl : List (String × Row)) : Bool :=
   206	  cl.any fun (t, r) => (referencing sch t).any fun (c, col, a) =>
   207	    a == .restrict && (s c).any fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k
   208	
   209	def clearCol (r : Row) (c : String) : Row :=
   210	  { r with cols := r.cols.map fun p => if p.1 == c then (p.1, Scalar.null) else p }
   211	
   212	/-- Clear every `set null` reference that names a closure row from outside it. -/
   213	def setNulls (sch : Schema) (cl : List (String × Row)) (s : Store) : Store :=
   214	  cl.foldl (fun s (t, r) => (referencing sch t).foldl (fun s (c, col, a) =>
   215	    if a == .setNull then
   216	      ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k).foldl
   217	        (fun s k => s.replaceRow c k (clearCol k col)) s
   218	    else s) s) s
   219	
   220	def storeSize (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat := sch.tables.foldl (fun n td => n + (s td.name).length) 0
   221	
   222	/-- The store after deleting `old` from `t` with its referential actions, or
   223	`E_REFERENCED`. With no action-carrying reference into `t`, exactly
   224	`removeRow` (LLP 3000.039 §1). -/
   225	def refDelete (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
   226	  let cl := closure sch s (storeSize sch s + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
   227	  if restricted sch s cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
   228	  else pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) (setNulls sch cl s))
   229	
   230	/-- Apply actions to the physical store using only the rows that are logically
   231	live as action witnesses. The root may itself be absent from `witnesses`. -/
   232	def refDeleteFrom (sch : Schema) (witnesses physical : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
   233	  let cl := closure sch witnesses (storeSize sch witnesses + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
   234	  if restricted sch witnesses cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
   235	  else

   237	      if action == .setNull then

   242	            | none => s) s
   243	      else s) s) physical

   261	def retireExpiredSameId (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) (t : String)

   274	  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none with
   275	  | some (_, r) => do
   276	    guardE (readableAt sch s v now t r) eRule
   277	    pure true
   278	  | none => pure false
   279	
   280	/-- An eager snapshot of the declared table rows used while sweeping. A
   281	`Store` update is a functional closure over the previous store; repeatedly
   282	retiring rows through that representation retains an exponentially growing
   283	evaluation tree. Snapshotting after each successful retirement changes only
   284	the representation, while preserving table order and action sequencing. -/
   285	abbrev MaterialStore := Array (String × List Row)
   286	
   287	def materialRows (tables : List String) (s : Store) : MaterialStore :=
   288	  tables.toArray.map fun t => (t, s t)
   289	
   290	def MaterialStore.store (rows : MaterialStore) (fallback : Store) : Store := fun t =>
   291	  match rows.find? fun p => p.1 == t with
   292	  | some (_, rs) => rs
   293	  | none => fallback t
   294	
   295	/-- Runtime's stable ancestor order is lexical when read-through is absent,
   296	as it is in this model fragment. Expiry retirement visits that order in
   297	reverse so peers cannot depend on declaration or mutation order. -/
   298	def expiryRetirementTables (sch : Schema) : List TableDecl :=
   299	  sch.tables.mergeSort fun a b => String.compare a.name b.name != .lt
   300	
   301	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — sweep each due root transactionally in table order.
   302	/-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
   303	stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
   304	model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
   305	root can be retired immediately. -/
   306	def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
   307	  let tables := sch.tables.map (·.name)
   308	  let rows := (expiryRetirementTables sch).foldl (fun rows td =>
   309	    let physical := rows.store s
   310	    let candidates := match td.expire with
   311	      | some column => sortRows [column] false (physical td.name)
   312	      | none => physical td.name
   313	    candidates.foldl (fun rows r =>
   314	      let physical := rows.store s
   315	      if expired td now r && stored physical td.name r then
   316	        match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch physical now) physical td.name r with
   317	        | .ok next => materialRows tables next
   318	        | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => rows
   319	        | .error _ => rows
   320	      else rows) rows) (materialRows tables s)
   321	  rows.store s
   322	
   323	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — same-id replacement authorizes, retires with actions, then inserts.
   324	/-- Apply one write to the store. -/
   325	def applyWrite (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Except Stop (Value × Store)
   326	  | .insert t fields ifAbsent =>
   327	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   328	    | none => throw eInput
   329	    | some td => do
   330	      let fs ← scalarsE fields
   331	      let rid ← insertId fs
   332	      let img ← buildImage td rid fs eInput
   333	      -- Native refusal order authorizes the proposed image while the expired
   334	      -- predecessor is still present, then retires it and applies its actions.
   335	      guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) eRule
   336	      if ifAbsent then
   337	        let clashes ← insertIfAbsentClash cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img
   338	        if clashes then pure (.null, s)
   339	        else
   340	          let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   341	          doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img eRule
   342	      else
   343	        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   344	        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img eRule
   345	  | .update t key patch cond =>
   346	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   347	    | none => throw eInput
   348	    | some td => do
   349	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   350	      let ps ← scalarsE patch
   351	      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
   352	      | none => throw notFound
   353	      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps cond
   354	  | .upsert t key patch =>
   355	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   356	    | none => throw eInput
   357	    | some td => do
   358	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   359	      let ps ← scalarsE patch
   360	      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
   361	      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps none
   362	      | none => do
   363	        let rid ← upsertId ks ps
   364	        let img ← buildImage td rid (ks ++ ps) notFound
   365	        guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) notFound
   366	        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   367	        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img notFound
   368	  | .delete t key =>
   369	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   370	    | none => throw eInput
   371	    | some td => do
   372	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   373	      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
   374	      | none => throw notFound
   375	      | some old => do
   376	        guardE (td.delete.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some old })
   377	          (if readableAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t old then eRule else notFound)
   378	        guardE ((referencing cx.schema t).isEmpty || readableAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t old) notFound
   379	        pure (.null, ← refDeleteFrom cx.schema (unexpiredStore cx.schema s cx.now) s t old)
   380	
   381	end Quarry
     1	import Quarry.Write
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Running a program
     5	
     6	`run` takes (schema, helpers, store, viewer, program, arguments, ceiling)
     7	to an outcome. This is the function the later harness oracle calls.
     8	-/
     9	
    10	namespace Quarry
    11	
    12	/-- An outcome. A query answers with data, `complete` and the returned
    13	page's continuation (`next`, null when none), or is unavailable (a cut
    14	scalar read), or refuses. A mutation commits a result and a new store, or
    15	refuses (and changes nothing). -/
    16	inductive Outcome where
    17	  | answer (data : Value) (complete : Bool) (next : Value)
    18	  | unavailable
    19	  | committed (result : Value) (store : Store)
    20	  | refused (code : String)
    21	
    22	/-- The world of a query: the view; every write refuses. -/
    23	def queryHooks : Hooks View where
    24	  view _ vw := vw
    25	  apply _ _ _ := throw (.refuse "E_QUARRY_PLACEMENT")
    26	
    27	/-- The world of a mutation: the store; reads see its visible rows. -/
    28	def storeHooks : Hooks Store where
    29	  view cx s := visibleRowsAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now
    30	  apply := applyWrite
    31	
    32	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — born-expired and updated-expired final images retire in the writer transaction.
    33	/-- Rows whose final images a mutation changed. Commit-end expiry retirement
    34	is scoped to this set; pre-existing expired backlog remains for the ordinary
    35	sweep. -/
    36	abbrev ChangedRows := List (String × List Nat)
    37	
    38	structure MutationWorld where
    39	  store : Store
    40	  changed : ChangedRows := []
    41	
    42	/-- The explicit address of an insert-like write that reached its write arm.
    43	This retains a structurally identical expired replacement for commit-end
    44	retirement, while excluding `insert if absent` live-clash no-ops. -/
    45	def RWrite.changedExplicitId? (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)
    46	  | .insert t fields ifAbsent => do
    47	    let td ← cx.schema.table? t
    48	    let fs ← (scalarsE fields).toOption
    49	    let rid ← (insertId fs).toOption
    50	    let img ← (buildImage td rid fs eInput).toOption
    51	    if ifAbsent && (findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td cx.now))
    52	        (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none).isSome
    53	    then none
    54	    else some (t, rid)
    55	  | .upsert t key patch =>
    56	    match key.lookup "id" with
    57	    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    58	    | _ => match patch.lookup "id" with
    59	      | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    60	      | _ => none
    61	  | _ => none
    62	
    63	def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=
    64	  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => (after td.name).filterMap fun row =>
    65	    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
    66	    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
    67	    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)
    68	
    69	def mutationHooks : Hooks MutationWorld where
    70	  view cx w := visibleRowsAt cx.schema w.store cx.viewer cx.now
    71	  apply cx w rw := match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
    72	    | .error e => .error e
    73	    | .ok (value, store) =>
    74	      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
    75	      let changed := match rw.changedExplicitId? cx w.store with
    76	        | some address => changed ++ [address]
    77	        | none => changed
    78	      .ok (value, { store, changed := changed.eraseDups })
    79	
    80	/-- Runtime retires changed expiry rows in reverse through-table order, then
    81	ascending id order. Read-through tables are outside this model fragment, so
    82	its through order is the schema's lexical table order. -/
    83	def changedRetirementOrder (sch : Schema) (changed : ChangedRows) : ChangedRows :=
    84	  (expiryRetirementTables sch).flatMap fun td =>
    85	    (changed.filter fun address => address.1 == td.name).mergeSort fun a b =>
    86	      lex cmpNat a.2 b.2 != .gt
    87	
    88	/-- Retire only rows written by this mutation whose final image is already
    89	expired. A restrict refusal aborts the mutation; cascade and set-null actions
    90	are in the same transition. -/
    91	def retireExpiredChanged (sch : Schema) (now : Int) : Store → ChangedRows → Except Stop Store
    92	  | s, [] => pure s
    93	  | s, (t, rid) :: rest =>
    94	    match sch.table? t with
    95	    | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
    96	    | some td =>
    97	      match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
    98	      | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
    99	      | some row =>
   100	        if expired td now row then do
   101	          let s ← refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t row
   102	          retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
   103	        else retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
   104	
   105	def bindArgs (params : List Param) (args : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop Env :=
   106	  params.mapM fun p => match args.lookup p.name with
   107	    | some v => pure (p.name, (v, none))
   108	    | none => if p.optional then pure (p.name, (.null, none)) else throw (.refuse "E_INPUT")
   109	
   110	def defaultFuel : Nat := 100000
   111	
   112	structure Case where
   113	  schema : Schema
   114	  helpers : List Helper := []
   115	  store : Store
   116	  viewer : List Nat
   117	  now : Int := 0
   118	  program : Program
   119	  args : List (String × Value) := []
   120	  budget : Option Nat := none
   121	  /-- Run only the server expiry sweep and return its resulting store. -/
   122	  sweepOnly : Bool := false
   123	
   124	def Case.ctx (c : Case) : Ctx :=
   125	  { schema := c.schema, viewer := c.viewer, now := c.now, helpers := c.helpers, budget := c.budget,
   126	    mutation := c.program.kind == .mutation }
   127	
   128	def flowValue : Flow → Value × Value
   129	  | .normal => (.null, .null)
   130	  | .ret v nx => (v, nx.getD .null)
   131	
   132	def runQuery (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   133	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   134	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   135	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   136	  | .ok env =>
   137	    let vw := visibleRowsAt c.schema c.store c.viewer c.now
   138	    match (execStmts queryHooks defaultFuel c.ctx vw env c.program.body).run {} with
   139	    | .ok ((fl, _, _), rs) => let (v, nx) := flowValue fl; .answer v rs.complete nx
   140	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   141	    | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   142	
   143	def runMutation (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   144	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   145	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   146	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   147	  | .ok env =>
   148	    match (execStmts mutationHooks defaultFuel c.ctx { store := c.store } env c.program.body).run {} with
   149	    | .ok ((fl, w, _), _) => match retireExpiredChanged c.schema c.now w.store
   150	        (changedRetirementOrder c.schema w.changed) with
   151	      | .ok s' => .committed (flowValue fl).1 s'
   152	      | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   153	      | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"
   154	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   155	    | .error .unavailable => .refused "E_BOUND"
   156	
   157	def run (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   158	  if c.sweepOnly then .committed .null (sweepExpired c.schema c.store c.now)
   159	  else match c.program.kind with
   160	    | .query => runQuery c
   161	    | .mutation => runMutation c
   162	
   163	end Quarry

     1	//! The engine against the Lean model (LLP 3000.035 §5.2).
     2	//!
     3	//! **The model side.** Each case's surface program goes through
     4	//! `snapback4_lang::emit::lean` (the parsed tree, never the binder's IR) to
     5	//! the model's case JSON, and through `quarry-oracle` (`snapback4/lean`,
     6	//! `lake build`), one long-lived process per worker that answers one tagged
     7	//! outcome per line. A case the emitter cannot translate is `Unsupported`
     8	//! under the emitter's named reason, never a pass.
     9	//!
    10	//! **The engine side.** The engine over SQLite (the ordinary in-memory
    11	//! server store) at `Ceilings::default()`, the ceilings a production server
    12	//! runs, not the case's stored budget; the model runs unbounded (its meter is
    13	//! abstract, OPEN M1).
    14	//!
    15	//! **Compared fields** (README, "How the harness compares"):
    16	//!
    17	//! - `kind`: answer, unavailable, refused, committed;
    18	//! - `code`: the refusal code (sites are not modelled);
    19	//! - `data` / `result`: exact, both sides as tagged values, so an id never
    20	//!   compares equal to a text (OPEN V1); rows compare as field maps;
    21	//! - `complete`: exact;
    22	//! - `next`: presence only (OPEN C1). When both carry one, each side
    23	//!   continues from its own cursor and the next page is compared
    24	//!   (`continuation-*`), until both are exhausted;
    25	//! - a mutation then runs `observe` on each side's resulting store
    26	//!   (`post-*`): the engine's store, and the model's committed store (or the
    27	//!   original store after a refusal).
    28	//!
    29	//! Meter fields, cut sites, `tables` and `seq` are not compared. Expiry
    30	//! sweeps advance both stores before the following program is compared.
    31	//!
    32	//! **Signatures** are `lean--{field}--{engine}~{model}`, each side's stable
    33	//! class (a refusal code, `unavailable`, `committed`, or the data's shape).
    34	//! The finding's `left` is the engine's raw record, `right` the model's raw
    35	//! outcome; the canonical forms compared are its `continuation`.
    36	// @ref LLP 3000.035#52-stage-2-a-small-lean-core — the Lean model as a further oracle over the Stage 1 generator.
    37	use crate::{

    56	/// The `quarry-oracle` executable: `SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE`, else the Lake
    57	/// build in this checkout.
    58	pub fn oracle_path() -> PathBuf {
    59	    match std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE") {
    60	        Some(p) => PathBuf::from(p),
    61	        None => PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../lean/.lake/build/bin/quarry-oracle"),
    62	    }
    63	}
    64	
    65	/// Bring this checkout's `quarry-oracle` up to date with its model sources
    66	/// (`lake build quarry-oracle`, under a second when current). A merge or
    67	/// checkout that changes `lean/` leaves the previous executable in `.lake`,
    68	/// and the harness would report that older model's choices as disagreements
    69	/// (2026-10-12: a stale pre-guard oracle on the merged `sb4-loop` tree showed
    70	/// `lean--complete--complete~incomplete`). Nothing is done when
    71	/// `SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE` names the oracle (the caller vouches for it; a
    72	/// campaign's workers inherit the refreshed path that way) or when `lake` is
    73	/// not installed (a missing oracle still refuses at `LeanProcess::spawn`).
    74	pub fn refresh() -> Result<(), String> {
    75	    if std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE").is_some() {
    76	        return Ok(());
    77	    }
    78	    let dir = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../lean");
    79	    // Keep the optional-tool path read-only, including a checkout whose model
    80	    // directory is not writable. A version probe writes no Lake build artifacts.
    81	    match Command::new("lake").arg("--version").current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    82	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
    83	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());
    84	            return Ok(());
    85	        }
    86	        Err(e) => return Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
    87	        Ok(_) => {} // The build below reports actual toolchain/configuration errors.
    88	    }
    89	    // @ref LLP 3000.035#52-stage-2-a-small-lean-core — concurrent refreshes must not write the same Lake artifacts.
    90	    let cache = dir.join(".lake");
    91	    fs::create_dir_all(&cache).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh cache: {e}"))?;
    92	    let refresh_lock = OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(false).read(true).write(true)
    93	        .open(cache.join("snapback4-refresh.lock")).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    94	    refresh_lock.lock().map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    95	    match Command::new("lake").args(["build", "quarry-oracle"]).current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    96	        Ok(output) if output.status.success() => Ok(()),
    97	        Ok(output) => Err(format!(
    98	            "`lake build quarry-oracle` failed in {}: {}{}",
    99	            dir.display(),
   100	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
   101	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
   102	        )),
   103	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
   104	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());
   105	            Ok(())
   106	        }
   107	        Err(e) => Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
   108	    }
   109	}

   111	/// One `quarry-oracle` process: a JSON case per line in, an outcome per line out.
   112	pub struct LeanProcess {
   113	    child: Child,
   114	    stdin: ChildStdin,
   115	    stdout: BufReader<ChildStdout>,
   116	}
   117	impl LeanProcess {
   118	    pub fn spawn() -> Result<Self, String> {
   119	        let path = oracle_path();
   120	        if !path.is_file() {
   121	            return Err(format!(
   122	                "Lean oracle missing: {} (run `cd snapback4/lean && lake build`, or set SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE)",
   123	                path.display()
   124	            ));
   125	        }
   126	        let mut child = Command::new(&path)
   127	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
   128	            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
   129	            .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
   130	            .spawn()
   131	            .map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
   132	        let stdin = child.stdin.take().unwrap();
   133	        let stdout = BufReader::new(child.stdout.take().unwrap());
   134	        Ok(Self { child, stdin, stdout })
   135	    }
   136	    pub fn ask(&mut self, case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   137	        writeln!(self.stdin, "{case}").map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle write: {e}"))?;
   138	        self.stdin.flush().map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle flush: {e}"))?;
   139	        let mut line = String::new();
   140	        let n = self.stdout.read_line(&mut line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle read: {e}"))?;
   141	        if n == 0 {
   142	            return Err("Lean oracle exited".into());
   143	        }
   144	        let answer: Json = serde_json::from_str(&line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle answer {line:?}: {e}"))?;
   145	        if answer["kind"] == "error" {
   146	            // A case the model cannot decode is an emitter defect, never a verdict.
   147	            return Err(format!("Lean oracle refused the case: {}", answer["error"]));
   148	        }
   149	        Ok(answer)
   150	    }
   151	}
   152	impl Drop for LeanProcess {
   153	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   154	        let _ = self.child.kill();
   155	        let _ = self.child.wait();
   156	    }
   157	}
   158	
   159	thread_local! {
   160	    static PROCESS: RefCell<Option<LeanProcess>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
   161	}
   162	
   163	/// Ask this thread's oracle process, starting it on first use and once
   164	/// more if it has died.
   165	pub fn ask(case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   166	    PROCESS.with(|cell| {
   167	        let mut slot = cell.borrow_mut();
   168	        if slot.is_none() {
   169	            *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   170	        }
   171	        match slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case) {
   172	            Err(e) if e == "Lean oracle exited" => {
   173	                *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   174	                slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case)
   175	            }
   176	            other => other,
   177	        }
   178	    })
   179	}
   180	
   181	/// The engine's value as the model's tagged value; rows as field maps.
   182	pub fn engine_value(v: &snapback4_core::Value) -> Json {
   183	    use snapback4_core::Value as V;
   184	    match v {
   185	        V::Null => json!({"null": null}),
   186	        V::Bool(b) => json!({"bool": b}),
   187	        V::Int(n) => json!({"int": n.to_string()}),
   188	        V::String(s) => json!({"text": s}),
   189	        V::Id(s) => json!({"id": s}),
   190	        V::Bytes(b) => json!({"bytes": b.iter().map(|x| format!("{x:02x}")).collect::<String>()}),
   191	        V::Row(fs) | V::Map(fs) => json!({"row": fs.iter().map(|(k, x)| (k.clone(), engine_value(x))).collect::<Map<_, _>>()}),
   192	        V::Array(xs) => json!({"arr": xs.iter().map(engine_value).collect::<Vec<_>>()}),
   193	    }
   194	}

   196	/// The model's tagged value with rows as field maps (its rows are ordered pairs).
   197	pub fn model_value(v: &Json) -> Json {
   198	    if let Some(xs) = v.get("arr").and_then(Json::as_array) {
   199	        return json!({"arr": xs.iter().map(model_value).collect::<Vec<_>>()});
   200	    }
   201	    if let Some(fs) = v.get("row").and_then(Json::as_array) {
   202	        let mut m = Map::new();
   203	        for p in fs {
   204	            m.insert(p[0].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned(), model_value(&p[1]));
   205	        }
   206	        return json!({"row": m});
   207	    }
   208	    v.clone()
   209	}

   211	fn shape(v: &Json) -> String {
   212	    v.as_object().and_then(|o| o.keys().next().cloned()).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".into())
   213	}

   215	/// One side's comparable record: `kind`, then `code` or `data`/`complete`/`next`.
   216	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
   217	pub struct Canon {
   218	    pub kind: String,
   219	    pub code: Option<String>,
   220	    pub data: Option<Json>,
   221	    pub complete: Option<bool>,
   222	    pub next: bool,
   223	}
   224	impl Canon {
   225	    /// The side's stable class for a differing `field`: the field's own
   226	    /// value where it is a flag, else a code, kind or data shape.
   227	    pub fn class(&self, field: &str) -> String {
   228	        if field.ends_with("complete") {
   229	            return if self.complete == Some(true) { "complete" } else { "incomplete" }.into();
   230	        }
   231	        if field.ends_with("next") {
   232	            return if self.next { "next" } else { "no-next" }.into();
   233	        }
   234	        match (&self.code, &self.data) {
   235	            (Some(code), _) => code.clone(),
   236	            (None, Some(d)) if self.kind == "answer" => shape(d),
   237	            _ => self.kind.clone(),
   238	        }
   239	    }
   240	    fn json(&self) -> Json {
   241	        json!({"kind": self.kind, "code": self.code, "data": self.data, "complete": self.complete, "next": self.next})
   242	    }
   243	}
   244	
   245	pub fn engine_canon(o: &Outcome) -> Canon {
   246	    let blank = Canon { kind: String::new(), code: None, data: None, complete: None, next: false };
   247	    if let Some(r) = o.refusal() {
   248	        return Canon { kind: "refused".into(), code: r["code"].as_str().map(str::to_owned), ..blank };
   249	    }
   250	    if o.kind == "mutation" {
   251	        let result = serde_json::from_value::<snapback4_core::Value>(o.value["result"].clone()).map(|v| engine_value(&v)).unwrap_or(Json::Null);
   252	        return Canon { kind: "committed".into(), data: Some(result), ..blank };
   253	    }
   254	    if o.value.get("unavailable") == Some(&json!(true)) {
   255	        return Canon { kind: "unavailable".into(), ..blank };
   256	    }
   257	    let data = serde_json::from_value::<snapback4_core::Value>(o.value["data"].clone()).map(|v| engine_value(&v)).unwrap_or(Json::Null);
   258	    Canon { kind: "answer".into(), data: Some(data), complete: o.value["complete"].as_bool(), next: o.next().is_some(), ..blank }
   259	}
   260	
   261	pub fn model_canon(m: &Json) -> Canon {
   262	    let blank = Canon { kind: m["kind"].as_str().unwrap_or("error").to_owned(), code: None, data: None, complete: None, next: false };
   263	    match blank.kind.as_str() {
   264	        "refused" => Canon { code: m["code"].as_str().map(str::to_owned), ..blank },
   265	        "committed" => Canon { data: Some(model_value(&m["result"])), ..blank },
   266	        "answer" => Canon {
   267	            data: Some(model_value(&m["data"])),
   268	            complete: m["complete"].as_bool(),
   269	            next: m["next"] != json!({"null": null}),
   270	            ..blank
   271	        },
   272	        _ => blank,
   273	    }
   274	}
   275	
   276	/// The first differing field, in the order a reader wants it.
   277	pub fn differ(e: &Canon, m: &Canon) -> Option<&'static str> {
   278	    if e.kind != m.kind {
   279	        return Some("kind");
   280	    }
   281	    if e.code != m.code {
   282	        return Some("code");
   283	    }
   284	    if e.data != m.data {
   285	        return Some(if e.kind == "committed" { "result" } else { "data" });
   286	    }
   287	    if e.complete != m.complete {
   288	        return Some("complete");
   289	    }
   290	    if e.next != m.next {
   291	        return Some("next");
   292	    }
   293	    None
   294	}
   295	
   296	/// `lean--{field}--{engine class}~{model class}`.
   297	pub fn signature(field: &str, e: &Canon, m: &Canon) -> String {
   298	    format!("lean--{}--{}~{}", field.replace('_', "-"), e.class(field), m.class(field))
   299	}
   300	
   301	fn finding(field: &str, e: &Canon, m: &Canon, engine: Outcome, model: &Json, trail: Vec<Outcome>) -> Verdict {
   302	    Verdict::Disagree(Finding {
   303	        signature: signature(field, e, m),
   304	        oracle: Oracle::Lean,
   305	        field: field.into(),
   306	        left: engine,
   307	        right: Outcome { kind: "lean".into(), value: model.clone() },
   308	        continuation: trail,
   309	        store_trace: None,
   310	    })
   311	}
   312	
   313	fn trail_entry(e: &Canon, m: &Canon) -> Outcome {
   314	    Outcome { kind: "canonical".into(), value: json!({"engine": e.json(), "model": m.json()}) }
   315	}

    53	// Add a capability and its schema predicate here in one line. This is both
    54	// the derivation and the decoder's allowlist; authors never declare it.
    55	const CAPABILITIES: &[(&str, fn(&Schema) -> bool)] = &[
    56	    ("source-write-reservations-v2", |s| s.source_reservations.values().any(|p| p.birth.is_some())),
    57	    ("source-write-reservations-v1", |s| !s.source_reservations.is_empty()),
    58	    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — older devices must not execute newly eligible
    59	    // writes using their receipt-derived maintenance path.
    60	    ("receipt-derived-prediction-v1", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| s.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target))
    61	        || s.has_receipt_columns()),
    62	    ("rule-reference-v2", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t|
    63	        [&t.rules.insert, &t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| r.any_term(&|term| matches!(term, RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. })))
    64	        || t.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { key, .. } if key.iter().any(|term| term.reference_source().is_some()))))),
    65	    ("rule-reference", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| [&t.rules.insert, &t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| r.has_reference()))),
    66	    ("declarative-receipts-v4", |s| !s.receipts.is_empty()),
    67	    ("owner-key-coverage", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.own_keys.is_some())),
    68	    ("ephemeral", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.ephemeral.is_some())),
    69	    ("field-authority", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.written_by.is_empty() || t.update_transition)),
    70	    // @ref LLP 3000.036#11 — an older decoder refuses ordered insert rules rather than misjudging them.
    71	    ("insert-rule-order", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| ordered(&t.rules.insert))),
    72	    // @ref LLP 3000.036#12 — a decoder that orders only int/time in insert rules refuses a money or decimal order by name.
    73	    ("insert-rule-order-units", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| ordered_units(t, &t.rules.insert))),
    74	    ("row-keyed-view", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m|m.row_key.is_some())),
    75	    // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#30-aggregate-target-identity-and-migration — older devices compute canonical-JSON
    76	    // aggregate ids and would silently miss digest-addressed target rows.
    77	    ("maintained-id-sha256-v1", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.row_key.is_none())),
    78	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#8 — an older engine or device must not delete with the old (orphaning) semantics.
    79	    ("reference-actions", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.on_delete.is_empty())),
    80	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — pre-Wave-12 devices neither retire expiry
    81	    // through actions nor queue an unproved same-id physical predecessor.
    82	    ("expiry-reference-actions-v1", |s| s.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.is_expiring() && s.is_referenced(name))),
    83	    ("read-through", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.through.is_some()) || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.parent_key.is_some() || !m.aliases.is_empty())),
    84	    // Device projections keep column metadata but omit private maintains.
    85	    ("maintained-column", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.maintained.is_empty()) || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.private.is_some())),
    86	    ("recorded-attribution", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.recorded.is_empty())),
    87	    ("sequence-by", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.sequences.is_empty())),
    88	    // @ref LLP 3000.040#4-fences-and-compatibility — an older decoder names the bounded int it cannot check.
    89	    ("int-range", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.values().any(int_range))),
    90	    // @ref LLP 3000.040#4-fences-and-compatibility — civil keys and calendar schedules.
    91	    ("calendar-month", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.indexes.values().any(|i| i.components.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, IndexComponent::Calendar(key) if key.civil()))))
    92	        || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.computed.values().any(|key| key.civil()))),
    93	    ("calendar-schedule", |s| s.schedules.iter().any(|schedule| schedule.months > 0)),
    94	    ("timeline", |s| s.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.version == 1)),
    95	    ("timeline-v2", |s| s.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.version == 2)),
    96	    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#3 — an older device would page a merged plan as an eager merge and refuse its server cursors; it refuses the backend by name.
    97	    ("branch-merge-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_merge)),
    98	    ("branch-membership-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership)),
    99	    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#15 — v2 fences metered uncapped discovery and row-id point lanes from v1 devices.
   100	    ("branch-pages-v2", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v2)),
   101	    ("branch-pages-v3", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v3)),
   102	    ("branch-pages-v4", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v4)),
   103	    ("branch-membership-v2", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership_v2)),
   104	    // Source slots alter negative coverage, prediction and application row projection.
   105	    ("timeline-event-slots", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.keys().any(|field| timeline::is_slot(field)))),
   106	    // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#2.3 — a decoder that ignored `also` would hold only the first arm and lose rows.
   107	    ("union-audience", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(Sync::is_union))),
   108	    ("time-audiences-v1", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.not_before.is_some())),
   109	];
   110	
   111	fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
   112	    match kind {
   113	        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
   114	        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
   115	        _ => false,
   116	    }
   117	}
   118	
   119	fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   120	    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
   121	    match rule {
   122	        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
   123	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
   124	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
   125	        _ => false,
   126	    }
   127	}
   128	
   129	fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   130	    match rule {
   131	        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
   132	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
   133	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
   134	        _ => false,
   135	    }
   136	}
   137	
   138	impl Schema {
   139	    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
   140	    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
   141	        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
   142	            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
   143	    }
   144	    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
   145	        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
   146	    }
   147	}
   148	
   149	impl Serialize for Schema {
   150	    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
   151	        let required = self.required_capabilities();
   152	        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
   153	        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
   154	        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
   155	        let mut wire = self.clone();
   156	        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
   157	            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
   158	        }
   159	        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
   160	            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
   161	        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
   162	        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
   163	    }
   164	}
   165	
   166	impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
   167	    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
   168	        // The private remote derive uses the ordinary
   169	        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.
   170	        let mut schema = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
   171	        let mut declared = BTreeSet::new();
   172	        let mut carriers = 0;
   173	        let mut legacy = false;
   174	        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
   175	            let mut recorded = 0;
   176	            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
   177	                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
   178	                    carriers += 1;
   179	                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
   180	                    false
   181	                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
   182	                    recorded += 1;
   183	                    false
   184	                } else { true }
   185	            });
   186	            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
   187	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
   188	            }
   189	            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
   190	        }
   191	        for name in &declared {
   192	            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
   193	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
   194	            }
   195	        }
   196	        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
   197	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
   198	        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
   199	        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
   200	        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
   201	        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
   202	            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
   203	        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
   204	        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
   205	        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
   206	            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
   207	            else { required.remove(cap); }
   208	        }
   209	        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
   210	        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
   211	        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
   212	        let mut legacy_semantic_capabilities = BTreeSet::new();
   213	        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1")
   214	            && required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
   215	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("maintained-id-sha256-v1".into());
   216	        }
   217	        // Kept pre-Wave-12 schemas need the server's new expiry action path,
   218	        // then stamp the device fence on their next published projection.
   219	        if !declared.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1")
   220	            && required.remove("expiry-reference-actions-v1") {
   221	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("expiry-reference-actions-v1".into());
   222	        }
   223	        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
   224	        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
   225	        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
   226	        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
   227	        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
   228	            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
   229	            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
   230	            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
   231	                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
   232	        }
   233	        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
   234	            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
   235	        }
   236	        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
   237	        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
   238	        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
   239	        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
   240	        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
   241	        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
   242	            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
   243	        schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities = legacy_semantic_capabilities.into();
   244	        Ok(schema)
   245	    }
   246	}

diff --git a/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Write.lean b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Write.lean
index 3d88e25806..7a48198c25 100644
--- a/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Write.lean
+++ b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Write.lean
@@ -98,6 +98,13 @@ def clashCode (td : TableDecl) (withId : Bool) (i : Nat) : Stop :=
 def findRow (rows : List Row) (ks : List (String × Scalar)) : Option Row :=
   if ks.any (·.2 == .null) then none else rows.find? (keyMatch ks)
 
+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#7 — expired rows release every logical lookup key.
+/-- A write target lookup selects among live rows, rather than selecting a
+physical predecessor and rejecting it after it has hidden a live match. -/
+def findLiveRow (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (rows : List Row)
+    (ks : List (String × Scalar)) : Option Row :=
+  findRow (rows.filter (unexpired td now)) ks
+
 /-- The result of a write: the row if the viewer can read it afterwards,
 else null (`why E_CONFLICT`: results are read-rule gets; OPEN W4 for insert). -/
 def resultOf (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=
@@ -311,18 +318,16 @@ def applyWrite (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Except Stop (Value × Store)
     | some td => do
       let ks ← scalarsE key
       let ps ← scalarsE patch
-      match findRow (s t) ks with
+      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
       | none => throw notFound
-      | some old => do
-        guardE (unexpired td cx.now old) notFound
-        doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps cond
+      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps cond
   | .upsert t key patch =>
     match cx.schema.table? t with
     | none => throw eInput
     | some td => do
       let ks ← scalarsE key
       let ps ← scalarsE patch
-      match findRow ((s t).filter (unexpired td cx.now)) ks with
+      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
       | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps none
       | none => do
         let rid ← upsertId ks ps
@@ -335,10 +340,9 @@ def applyWrite (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Except Stop (Value × Store)
     | none => throw eInput
     | some td => do
       let ks ← scalarsE key
-      match findRow (s t) ks with
+      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
       | none => throw notFound
       | some old => do
-        guardE (unexpired td cx.now old) notFound
         guardE (td.delete.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some old })
           (if readableAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t old then eRule else notFound)
         guardE ((referencing cx.schema t).isEmpty || readableAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t old) notFound

     for (name, (schema, types)) in actual {
-        if strip_update_explanations(&schema) != expected[&name].0 { mismatches.push(format!("schema bytes: {name}")); }
+        let normalized = strip_update_explanations(&schema);

         let types = strip_following(&strip_row_keys(&strip_hook_hints(&types)), &schema);

@@ -217,7 +218,22 @@ fn strip_update_explanations(text: &str) -> String {

         }
     }
-    serde_json::to_string(&schema).unwrap()
+    let wire = serde_json::to_string(&schema).unwrap();
+    // P2 derives this fence from ordinary maintains, so Schema serialization
+    // restores it even after typed normalization. Remove only that named flag
+    // from the final wire image for this pre-P2 compatibility corpus.
+    strip_maintained_identity_capability(wire)
+}
+
+fn strip_maintained_identity_capability(mut wire: String) -> String {
+    let capability = "maintained-id-sha256-v1";
+    wire = wire.replace(&format!("\"{capability}\","), "")
+        .replace(&format!(",\"{capability}\""), "")
+        .replace(&format!("[{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}}]"), "[]")
+        .replace(&format!("{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}},"), "")
+        .replace(&format!(",{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}}"), "");
+    assert!(!wire.contains(capability));
+    wire
 }

 llp/3000.007.003-the-engine-writes-derived-data.rfc.md | 6 ++++++
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)

diff --git a/llp/3000.007.003-the-engine-writes-derived-data.rfc.md b/llp/3000.007.003-the-engine-writes-derived-data.rfc.md
index 56fc7db327..dbcb74a3df 100644

+++ b/llp/3000.007.003-the-engine-writes-derived-data.rfc.md
@@ -139,6 +139,12 @@ identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
 adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
 address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
 
+The intrinsic `byId` order of aggregate rows is consequently opaque digest
+order. It is stable for one identity version but has no relationship to the
+lexical or numeric order of group fields, and migration may change it. A query
+whose result needs group-key order declares that order explicitly (for example,
+`first 50 by .emoji`) rather than relying on an unqualified aggregate scan.
+
 The SQLite metadata and evaluation-PostgreSQL backend marker
 `maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` bind persisted aggregate targets to that
 function. Opening or adopting either store without the marker — including a
