   438	
   439	// One lifecycle boundary for every private publication key: deferred cursor,
   440	// effects/receipts, request capture, snapshot keys and staged rows always clear.
   441	// keep_images controls only published replay evidence, never private progress.
   442	fn reset_publication<T: DeviceTx>(tx: &T, keep_images: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   443	    deferred::clear(tx)?;
   444	    predictions::reset(tx, keep_images)?;
   445	    snapshot::clear(tx)
   446	}
   447	
   448	impl<S: DeviceStore> Device<S> {
   449	    /// The device over an opened store, for the backend the server sent —
   450	    /// or, with none, for the backend kept from last time, so a device
   451	    /// that starts with no network opens on what it holds. The schema is
   452	    /// installed; a literal-default addition can keep older row images.
   453	    pub fn open_store(store: S, backend: Option<Backend>) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
   454	        Self::open_store_mode(store, backend, false)
   455	    }
   456	
   457	    /// Open the kept backend, installing the supplied one only if still empty.
   458	    /// A concurrent installer may win; it must never lose its replica evidence.
   459	    pub fn open_store_initial(store: S, backend: Backend) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
   460	        Self::open_store_mode(store, Some(backend), true)
   461	    }
   462	
   463	    #[allow(unreachable_code)] fn open_store_mode(mut store: S, backend: Option<Backend>, initial: bool) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
   464	        let kept = store.meta(BACKEND)?;
   465	        // Every opening must understand the saved schema before replacing it,
   466	        // including an explicit backend. Installation checks this same capture.
   467	        // An explicit first install has no saved backend to protect. Preserve
   468	        // the ordinary install contract there; conditional first installs must
   469	        // still compare absence, and every reopening compares the checked bytes.
   470	        let expected = if initial || backend.is_none() || kept.is_some() {
   471	            BTreeMap::from([(BACKEND.to_owned(), kept.clone())])
   472	        } else { BTreeMap::new() };

   474	            .map_err(|e| RuntimeError::decode(e, |e| RuntimeError::Store(format!("the kept backend does not parse: {e}")))))
   475	            .transpose()?;
   476	        if let Some(previous) = &previous { check_version(&previous.schema)?; }
   477	        let kept_needs_semantic_upgrade = previous.as_ref().is_some_and(|backend|
   478	            !backend.schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities.is_empty());
   479	        let mut backend = if backend.is_none() || (initial && kept.is_some() && !kept_needs_semantic_upgrade) {
   480	            previous.clone().ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Auth("this device has never synced: the server must be reachable once to open".into()))?
   481	        } else { backend.unwrap() };
   482	        check_version(&backend.schema)?;
   483	        backend.require_current_semantics()?;
   484	        backend.schema.check_row_view_audiences()?;
   485	        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
   486	        {

   488	                return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_VIEW_KEY", message: issue.message });
   489	            }
   490	            for program in &backend.programs { snapback4_core::engine::admission::check_state_predicates(&backend.schema, program)?; }

   493	        let held = store.meta(GENERATION)?.and_then(|g| g.parse::<u64>().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
   494	        let reset = held != 0 && held != backend.generation;

   496	        let keep_images = false;
   497	        let keep_acquired = false;
   498	        let backend_identity = store_identity::backend_identity(&backend);
   499	        let mut metadata = BTreeMap::from([(BACKEND.to_owned(), encoded(&backend)?), (GENERATION.to_owned(), backend.generation.to_string()), (BACKEND_IDENTITY.to_owned(), backend_identity.clone())]);
   500	        if reset {

   503	            invalidate_native(&mut metadata);
   504	            metadata.insert(history::GROUPS.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   505	            metadata.insert(history::STAGED_GROUPS.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   506	            metadata.insert(boundary::STAGED.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   507	            if !keep_acquired { metadata.insert(boundary::BOUNDARIES.to_owned(), "{}".into()); }

   510	        store.install_checked(&backend.schema, &metadata, reset && !keep_images, &expected)?;

   523	            (Some(hex), Some(digest), Some(generation)) if generation.parse::<u64>().ok() == Some(backend.generation) => snapback4_core::value::decode_bytes_hex(hex)

   540	        let store_identity = store.meta(STORE_ID)?;

   543	            schema: backend.schema,
   544	            programs: snapback4_core::small_map::collect(backend.programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p))),
   545	            generation: backend.generation,
   546	            backend_identity,
   547	            store_identity,
   548	            snapshot_owner: None,

   554	
   555	    /// Install the app's native module the server serves at `/native.wasm`
   556	    /// (LLP 3000.005 §9), keeping its bytes so a cold start offline has it.
   557	    /// Returns the jobs and the reads it implements.
   558	    pub fn install_native(&mut self, bytes: &[u8], digest: &str, generation: u64) -> Result<(Vec<String>, Vec<String>), RuntimeError> {
   559	        if generation != self.generation {
   560	            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the native module belongs to an obsolete backend generation".into()));
   561	        }
   562	        #[cfg(feature = "wasm-host")]
   563	        {
   564	            if sha256(bytes) != digest {
   565	                return Err(RuntimeError::Native { code: "E_NATIVE".into(), message: "the native module does not match its SHA-256 digest".into() });
   566	            }
   567	            let module = snapback4_core::engine::native::Module::compile(bytes)?;
   568	            let names = (module.jobs().to_vec(), module.reads().to_vec());
   569	            let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
   570	            store_identity::require_backend(&tx, &self.backend_identity, &self.store_identity)?;
   571	            store_identity::require_healthy(&tx)?;
   572	            if tx.meta(BACKEND_REQUIRED)?.is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty()) {
   573	                return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("this store's backend has not been adopted; reconnect to acquire it".into()));
   574	            }
   575	            tx.set_meta(NATIVE, &snapback4_core::value::encode_bytes_hex(bytes))?;
   576	            tx.set_meta(NATIVE_DIGEST, digest)?;
   577	            tx.set_meta(NATIVE_GENERATION, &generation.to_string())?;
   578	            tx.commit()?;
   579	            self.native = Some(std::sync::Arc::new(module));
   580	            self.native_digest = Some(digest.to_owned());
   581	            Ok(names)
   582	        }
   583	        #[cfg(not(feature = "wasm-host"))]
   584	        {
   585	            let _ = (bytes, digest);
   586	            Err(RuntimeError::Native { code: "E_NATIVE".into(), message: "this device was built without the wasm host; native reads go to the server".into() })
   587	        }
   588	    }
   589	
   590	    /// The digest of the module installed, as the server named it.
   591	    pub fn native_digest(&self) -> Option<&str> {
   592	        self.native_digest.as_deref()
   593	    }
   594	
   595	    /// The backend changed (a new generation from `/schema`): adopt it and
   596	    /// keep it. A changed generation replaces base images and requests a fresh snapshot.
   597	    pub fn adopt(&mut self, backend: Backend) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   598	        self.adopt_captured(backend, BTreeMap::new())
   599	    }
   600	
   601	    pub fn adopt_captured(&mut self, mut backend: Backend, mut expected: BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   602	        check_version(&backend.schema)?;
   603	        backend.require_current_semantics()?;
   604	        backend.schema.check_row_view_audiences()?;
   605	        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
   606	        {
   607	            if let Some(issue) = snapback4_core::schema::columns::validate(&backend.schema).into_iter().find(|i| i.message.contains("E_VIEW_KEY")) {
   608	                return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_VIEW_KEY", message: issue.message });
   609	            }
   610	            for program in &backend.programs { snapback4_core::engine::admission::check_state_predicates(&backend.schema, program)?; }
   611	        }
   612	        backend.schema.prepare_contribution_indexes();
   613	        let required = self.store.meta(BACKEND_REQUIRED)?;
   614	        expected.entry(BACKEND_REQUIRED.into()).or_insert(required.clone());
   615	        expected.entry(STORE_ID.into()).or_insert(self.store.meta(STORE_ID)?);
   616	        expected.entry(SEND_REVISION.into()).or_insert(self.store.meta(SEND_REVISION)?);
   617	        let adopted_store = expected.get(STORE_ID).cloned().flatten();
   618	        let cached_native = self.store.meta(NATIVE_DIGEST)?;
   619	        expected.entry(NATIVE_DIGEST.into()).or_insert(cached_native.clone());
   620	        let obsolete_native = adopted_store != self.store_identity || cached_native.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).as_deref() != self.native_digest.as_deref();
   621	        let replacement = required.as_ref().is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty());
   622	        let reset = backend.generation != self.generation;
   623	        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#91-per-row-narrowed-value-dormancy — schema shape alone cannot certify the release's active population.
   624	        let keep_images = false;
   625	        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#91-per-row-narrowed-value-dormancy — a release can hide restored data even when its added columns have literal defaults.
   626	        let keep_acquired = false;
   627	        let backend_identity = store_identity::backend_identity(&backend);
   628	        let mut metadata = BTreeMap::from([(BACKEND.to_owned(), encoded(&backend)?), (GENERATION.to_owned(), backend.generation.to_string()), (BACKEND_IDENTITY.to_owned(), backend_identity.clone())]);
   629	        metadata.insert(BACKEND_REQUIRED.to_owned(), String::new());
   630	        if reset {
   631	            metadata.insert(WATERMARK.to_owned(), "0".into());
   632	            metadata.insert(ACQUIRED.to_owned(), if keep_acquired { backend.generation.to_string() } else { String::new() });
   633	            invalidate_native(&mut metadata);
   634	            metadata.insert(history::GROUPS.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   635	            metadata.insert(history::STAGED_GROUPS.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   636	            metadata.insert(boundary::STAGED.to_owned(), "{}".into());
   637	            if !keep_acquired { metadata.insert(boundary::BOUNDARIES.to_owned(), "{}".into()); }
   638	        }
   639	        if replacement { invalidate_native(&mut metadata); }
   640	        self.store.install_checked(&backend.schema, &metadata, reset && !keep_images, &expected)?;
   641	        if reset || replacement || obsolete_native {
   642	            #[cfg(feature = "wasm-host")]
   643	            {
   644	                self.native = None;
   645	            }
   646	            self.native_digest = None;
   647	        }
   648	        self.schema = backend.schema;
   649	        self.programs = snapback4_core::small_map::collect(backend.programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)));
   650	        self.generation = backend.generation;
   651	        self.backend_identity = backend_identity;
   652	        self.store_identity = adopted_store;
   653	        self.snapshot_owner = None;
   654	        Ok(())
   655	    }

   657	    /// The watermark the device has applied through, and its generation.
   658	    pub fn state(&self) -> Result<(u64, u64), RuntimeError> {
   659	        Ok((self.store.meta(WATERMARK)?.and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0), self.generation))
   660	    }
   661	
   662	    /// Persist before starting a POST, so another owner of the store
   663	    /// cannot apply an older sync response that omitted the write being sent.
   664	    pub fn begin_send(&mut self) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   665	        self.begin_send_for(None)
   666	    }
   667	
   668	    pub fn begin_send_for(&mut self, id: Option<&str>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   669	        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
   670	        store_identity::require_healthy(&tx)?;
   671	        if id.is_none(){for data in tx.outbox_entries()?{upload::require_ready(&decoded::<Queued>(&data)?)?;}}
   672	        if let Some(id) = id {
   673	            if let Some(data) = tx.outbox_get(id)? {
   674	                let entry: Queued = decoded(&data)?;
   675	                upload::require_ready(&entry)?;
   676	                if entry.upload.as_ref().is_some_and(|u| u.get("store_id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != tx.meta(STORE_ID).ok().flatten().as_deref()) {
   677	                    return Err(RuntimeError::Structural {code:"E_STORE_REPLACED",message:"upload belongs to another backend store".into()});
   678	                }
   679	            }
   680	            predictions::dispatch(&tx, id, "")?;
   681	        }
   682	        let revision = meta_u64(&tx, SEND_REVISION)?.checked_add(1).filter(|n| *n <= 9_007_199_254_740_991).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("send revision overflow".into()))?;
   683	        tx.set_meta(SEND_REVISION, &revision.to_string())?;
   684	        // A send invalidates snapshot paging, but a terminal snapshot already
   685	        // owns a live catch-up cut. Keep it and bind future catch-up to this send.
   686	        let paging = tx.meta(SNAPSHOT_NEXT)?.is_some_and(|next| !next.is_empty());
   687	        if paging { snapshot::clear(&tx)?; }
   688	        else if tx.meta(SNAPSHOT_OWNER)?.is_some() { tx.set_meta(SNAPSHOT_SEND_REVISION, &revision.to_string())?; }
   689	        tx.commit()?;
   690	        if paging { self.snapshot_owner = None; }
   691	        Ok(revision)
   692	    }
   693	
   694	    pub fn hold_write(&mut self, id: &str, reason: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   695	        let tx = self.store.transaction()?;
   696	        predictions::dispatch(&tx, id, reason)?;
   697	        tx.commit()
   698	    }

   700	    /// What a sync request is made from: the watermark, the generation,
   701	    /// the writes sent but not yet seen, and the send revision.
   702	    pub fn sync_state(&mut self) -> Result<SyncState, RuntimeError> {
   703	        self.sync_state_inner(true)
   704	    }
   705	
   706	    /// Inspect current progress without declaring a new in-flight request.
   707	    pub fn sync_state_read(&mut self) -> Result<SyncState, RuntimeError> {
   708	        self.sync_state_inner(false)
   709	    }

   358	    let mut m_args = match module.tag_args("run", &case.args) {
   359	        Ok(a) => a,
   360	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),
   361	    };
   362	    // The prelude: each step on the engine and on the model's store, in order.
   363	    for i in 0..case.steps.len() {
   364	        if let Err(u) = module.program(&format!("prep{i}")) {
   365	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   366	        }
   367	        if let Err(u) = module.tag_args(&format!("prep{i}"), &case.steps[i].args) {
   368	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   369	        }
   370	    }
   371	    let (mut engine, prelude) = execute::world(case, source)?;
   372	    engine.set_ceilings(Ceilings::default());
   373	    let mut executed = 0;
   374	    let mut pages = 0;
   375	    let mut store = store;
   376	    let mut steps = prelude.iter();
   377	    let mut trail = vec![];
   378	    for (i, step) in case.steps.iter().enumerate() {
   379	        let name = format!("prep{i}");
   380	        if step.sweep {
   381	            let e_sweep = steps.next().ok_or("prelude sweep outcome missing")?;
   382	            if e_sweep.kind != "sweep" || e_sweep.value.get("error").is_some() {
   383	                return Err(format!("engine prelude sweep failed: {:?}", e_sweep.value));
   384	            }
   385	            let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   386	            let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);
   387	            let swept = ask(&module.case_at_sweep(&name, store.clone(), viewer, args, None, step.at, true).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   388	            executed += 1;
   389	            if swept["kind"] != "committed" { return Err(format!("Lean prelude sweep failed: {swept}")); }
   390	            store = swept["store"].clone();
   391	        }
   392	        let e_raw = steps.next().ok_or("prelude outcome missing")?.clone();
   393	        let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   394	        let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);
   395	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at(&name, store.clone(), viewer, args, None, step.at).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   396	        executed += 2;
   397	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   398	        trail.push(trail_entry(&e, &m));
   399	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   400	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("prelude-{f}"), &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   401	        }
   402	        if m.kind == "committed" {
   403	            store = m_raw["store"].clone();
   404	        }
   405	    }
   406	    if case.sweep {

   408	        if e_sweep.kind != "sweep" || e_sweep.value.get("error").is_some() {
   409	            return Err(format!("engine final sweep failed: {:?}", e_sweep.value));
   410	        }
   411	        let swept = ask(&module.case_at_sweep("run", store.clone(), &case.principal, m_args.clone(), None, case.clock, true).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   412	        executed += 1;
   413	        if swept["kind"] != "committed" { return Err(format!("Lean final sweep failed: {swept}")); }
   414	        store = swept["store"].clone();
   415	    }
   416	    if mutation {
   417	        let e_raw = execute::execute(&mut engine, case, "run", &case.args);
   418	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at("run", store.clone(), &case.principal, m_args, None, case.clock).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   419	        executed += 2;
   420	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   421	        let first_class = e.class("kind");
   422	        let mut trail = vec![trail_entry(&e, &m)];
   423	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   424	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(f, &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   425	        }
   426	        // The resulting stores, seen through `observe`.
   427	        let after = if m.kind == "committed" { m_raw["store"].clone() } else { store };
   428	        let o_args = module.tag_args("observe", &case.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   429	        let eo_raw = execute::execute(&mut engine, case, "observe", &case.args);
   430	        let mo_raw = ask(&module.case_at("observe", after, &case.principal, o_args, None, case.clock).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   431	        executed += 2;
   432	        let (eo, mo) = (engine_canon(&eo_raw), model_canon(&mo_raw));
   433	        trail.push(trail_entry(&eo, &mo));
   434	        if let Some(f) = differ(&eo, &mo) {
   435	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("post-{f}"), &eo, &mo, eo_raw, &mo_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   436	        }
   437	        return Ok(Checked { verdict: Verdict::Pass, executed, pages, mutation, class: format!("{}-{}", if mutation { "mutation" } else { "query" }, first_class) });
   438	    }
   439	    let mut e_args = case.args.clone();
   440	    let mut trail = Vec::new();
   441	    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
   442	    let mut first_class = String::new();
   443	    loop {
   444	        let e_raw = execute::execute(&mut engine, case, "run", &e_args);
   445	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at("run", store.clone(), &case.principal, m_args.clone(), None, case.clock).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   446	        executed += 2;
   447	        pages += 1;
   448	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   449	        if pages == 1 {
   450	            first_class = e.class("kind");
   451	        }
   452	        trail.push(trail_entry(&e, &m));
   453	        let phase = if pages > 1 { "continuation-" } else { "" };
   454	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   455	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("{phase}{f}"), &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   456	        }
   457	        if !e.next {
   458	            break;
   459	        }
   460	        let next = e_raw.next().unwrap().to_owned();
   461	        if !seen.insert(next.clone()) || seen.len() > case.rows.len() + 2 {
   462	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding("cursor-cycle", &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   463	        }
   464	        e_args["c"] = json!(next);
   465	        m_args.insert("c".into(), m_raw["next"].clone());
   466	    }
   467	    Ok(Checked { verdict: Verdict::Pass, executed, pages, mutation, class: format!("query-{first_class}") })
   468	}

   470	/// The open points a case can exercise (`snapback4/lean/OPEN.md`), counted
   471	/// over compared cases so a report shows each point's evidence.
   472	pub fn features(case: &Case) -> Vec<String> {
   473	    use crate::ast::{Read, Rule, Write};
   474	    let mut out = Vec::new();
   475	    out.extend(crate::generate::page4_features(case));
   476	    out.extend(crate::generate::page5_features(case));
   477	    let items = &case.program.tables[0];
   478	    let rules: Vec<Rule> = items.effects.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| vec![items.rule.clone(); 4]);
   479	    let access_hidden = case.program.tables.get(1).and_then(|t| t.effects.as_ref()).is_some_and(|e| e[0] == Rule::Deny);
   480	    let body = &case.program.body;
   481	    let write = match body {
   482	        Body::Write(w, _) => Some(w),
   483	        _ => None,
   484	    };
   485	    if items.effects.is_some() {
   486	        out.push("items-effect-rules".into());
   487	    }
   488	    // LLP 3000.036.001: branch pages (the merged plan is decided by OPEN C8's branch rule).
   489	    let where_branch = case.program.domain.as_deref().is_some_and(|domain| domain.contains(" or "));
   490	    if let Some(domain) = case.program.domain.as_ref().filter(|_| where_branch) {

   180	    /// edge multiplies by its cap, and edges into a table add up. `None` when
   181	    /// the cascade graph from `parent` is cyclic or a cascade lacks its cap.
   182	    pub fn closure_bounds(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Vec<(String, u64)>> {
   183	        // Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.
   184	        let mut reach: Vec<String> = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   185	        let mut edges: Vec<(usize, usize, u64)> = Vec::new();
   186	        let mut at = 0;
   187	        while at < reach.len() {
   188	            let table = reach[at].clone();
   189	            for r in self.referencing(&table) {
   190	                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
   191	                let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);
   192	                let child = reach.iter().position(|t| t == r.child).unwrap_or_else(|| { reach.push(r.child.to_owned()); reach.len() - 1 });
   193	                edges.push((at, child, cap));
   194	            }
   195	            at += 1;
   196	        }
   197	        // Kahn's order over the reached cascade subgraph; a leftover table is a cycle.
   198	        let mut indegree = vec![0_usize; reach.len()];
   199	        for &(_, child, _) in &edges { indegree[child] += 1; }
   200	        let mut bounds = vec![0_u64; reach.len()];
   201	        bounds[0] = 1;
   202	        let mut ready: Vec<usize> = (0..reach.len()).filter(|&t| indegree[t] == 0).collect();
   203	        let mut done = 0;
   204	        while let Some(table) = ready.pop() {
   205	            done += 1;
   206	            for &(from, child, cap) in edges.iter().filter(|(from, _, _)| *from == table) {
   207	                bounds[child] = bounds[child].saturating_add(bounds[from].saturating_mul(cap));
   208	                indegree[child] -= 1;
   209	                if indegree[child] == 0 { ready.push(child); }
   210	            }
   211	        }
   212	        (done == reach.len()).then(|| reach.into_iter().zip(bounds).collect())
   213	    }

   215	    /// The fixed charge a delete of a `parent` row reserves before it probes,
   216	    /// cascades or clears any row, over every meter: the closure's rows and
   217	    /// their identities, every restrict probe (one seek per closure row, plus
   218	    /// the closure rows it skips), every set-null row, and one engine write of
   219	    /// each, priced from the source-write plan the engine already exports. A
   220	    /// function of the schema only — caps, the reference graph, each table's
   221	    /// indexes and row size, and the exported plans — so a meter, an `E_BOUND`
   222	    /// abort or the physical allowance never depends on how many (hidden) rows
   223	    /// exist, and every host charges alike: a device's projection keeps every
   224	    /// table that can carry an action and every exported price. `None` when the
   225	    /// closure is unbounded (a cycle or a missing cap) or a written table has no
   226	    /// fixed write price. Heap is the closure's identity scratch plus the largest
   227	    /// single row's transient work, plus event images retained until commit.
   228	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — the reservation is schema-fixed; LLP 3000.015 §2's law for work shaped by hidden rows.
   229	    pub fn delete_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {

   233	        let mut identities = 0_u64;
   234	        let mut gathered = 0_u64;
   235	        let rows_of = |name: &str| bounds.iter().find(|(t, _)| t == name).map_or(0, |(_, n)| *n);
   236	        for (table, n) in &bounds {
   237	            let n = *n;
   238	            if table != parent {
   239	                // Fetched by the closure walk and again, current, before its delete.
   240	                let unit = self.unit_write(table)?;

   243	                identities = identities.saturating_add(n);
   244	                // Before any set-null write, each reached cascade row proves
   245	                // that no physically retained read-through child lies outside
   246	                // the closure. Each child table can skip every reached
   247	                // identity from that table and then inspect one outside
   248	                // witness. Execution performs
   249	                // these probes under reference_prepaid, so their complete
   250	                // schema bound belongs in this outer admission reservation.
   251	                let through_children: Vec<_> = self.children(table).collect();
   252	                let probes_per_row = through_children.iter()
   253	                    .map(|(child, _, _)| rows_of(child).saturating_add(1))
   254	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   255	                let probes = n.saturating_mul(probes_per_row);
   256	                add(&mut price, [probes, 0, probes, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   257	                let outside_heap = through_children.iter()
   258	                    .map(|(name, child, _)| crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(child).saturating_mul(rows_of(name).saturating_add(1)))
   259	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   260	                heap = heap.max(outside_heap);
   261	            }
   262	            for r in self.referencing(table) {
   263	                // A capped walk holds one page of child images per seek.
   264	                let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(r.table);
   265	                heap = heap.max(row.saturating_mul(REFERENCE_PAGE as u64));

   268	                let walk = |cap: u64| seeks * n + cap.saturating_mul(n) / REFERENCE_PAGE as u64;

   270	                // child, including children the closure already cascaded away.
   271	                let through = r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column);
   272	                if through && table != parent { add(&mut price, [3_u64, 0, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n))); }
   273	                match r.action {
   274	                    // A read-through child's probe: three seeks per closure row (LLP 3000.014 §6).
   275	                    OnDelete::Restrict if through => {},
   276	                    // One probe per closure row, a row per seek: it may skip the closure
   277	                    // rows that name it (each names one target per reference), then stops
   278	                    // at its first outside witness.
   279	                    OnDelete::Restrict => {
   280	                        let probe = seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n;
   281	                        add(&mut price, [2 * probe, probe, seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
   282	                    }
   283	                    OnDelete::Cascade => {
   284	                        let pages = walk(u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?));

   286	                    }

   288	                        let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);

   290	                        let cleared = cap.saturating_mul(n);
   291	                        let unit = self.unit_write(r.child)?;
   292	                        heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
   293	                        let pages = walk(cap);
   294	                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);

   296	                    }

   298	                }
   299	            }
   300	        }
   301	        // The root is read again, current, before its own removal.
   302	        price[2] = price[2].saturating_add(1);
   303	        // The closure's identities (table and id) are held until the last
   304	        // delete, with the root's and one page of child ids.
   305	        // A set-null group is gathered whole (at most its cap) before it is cleared.
   306	        price[4] = heap.saturating_add(identities.saturating_add(1 + REFERENCE_PAGE as u64 + gathered).saturating_mul(CLOSURE_IDENTITY_BYTES));

   312	        }

   315	        Some(price)
   316	    }

   331	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — two event images per priced row write, plus bounded keys and audience transitions, retained for the request lifetime.
   332	    fn retained_action_heap(&self, parent: &str, writes: u64) -> Option<u64> {
   333	        let mut per_write = 0;
   334	        for (table, _) in self.closure_bounds(parent)? {
   335	            for reference in self.referencing(&table) {
   336	                if reference.action.writes() {
   337	                    let events = self.write_reservation(reference.child)?.action_events?;
   338	                    per_write = per_write.max(events.heap_per_write);
   339	                }
   340	            }
   341	        }
   342	        Some(writes.saturating_mul(per_write))
   343	    }

   346	    /// write it, its index entries (a `words(..)` index at its token bound), a
   347	    /// row copy, and the source-write price the engine exports for the table.
   348	    fn unit_write(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   349	        let table = self.table(name)?;

   363	            add(&mut unit, plan.price(phase));
   364	        }

+This commit-end rule also covers a source of a row-keyed maintained view. The
+source's final image first reaches normal maintenance, then its expired image
+is retired through the common action path in the same transaction. No derived
+maintenance shortcut may physically remove that source before closure
+preflight: doing so would bypass a live `restrict` child and could orphan a
+`cascade` or `set null` child. The source contribution and its retirement
+cancel within the transaction, so an already-expired birth never enters a
+committed count basis. The execution retains at most one retirement key per
+changed source row; its allocation is charged when first retained and the
+program's existing rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
+
 A live `restrict` child, or a physically retained read-through child outside
 the cascade closure but below a row in it, keeps the expired root physically
 stored and the sweep continues to later due keys. A read-through child inside

+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/maintains.rs
@@ -18,6 +18,39 @@ fn target_group_key(maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Vec<Value> {
     if maintain.by.is_empty() { vec![Value::Bool(true)] } else { key.to_vec() }
 }
 
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match kind {
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+

+    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
+    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
+    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
+    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
+    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
+    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain]) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+        let mut legacy = Vec::new();
+        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
+            let target = self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].clone();
+            let fields: Vec<_> = maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
+                let kind = target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
+                (field, kind)
+            }).collect();
+            let mut rows = Vec::new();
+            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
+            loop {
+                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
+                if page.is_empty() { break; }
+                for (row, encoded) in page {
+                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
+                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
+                    let key = fields.iter().map(|(field, kind)| Ok((kind.clone(), row.field(field)?.clone())))
+                        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?;
+                    rows.push((old, key));
+                }
+            }
+            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
+        }
+
+        let mut ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
+        let mut settled = false;
+        for _ in 0..=legacy.len() {
+            let mut next_ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
+            for (target, rows) in &legacy {
+                let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
+                for (old, key) in rows {
+                    let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
+                        let mut value = value.clone();
+                        rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
+                        value
+                    }).collect();
+                    let next = maintained_id(&key);
+                    if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
+                }
+            }
+            if next_ids == ids {
+                ids = next_ids;
+                settled = true;
+                break;
+            }
+            ids = next_ids;
+        }
+        if !settled {
+            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()));
+        }
+
+        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
+            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
+                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
+                .collect();
+            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
+        }).collect();
+        let mut rewritten = 0_u64;
+        for (name, table, columns) in references {
+            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
+            loop {
+                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
+                if page.is_empty() { break; }
+                for (old, encoded) in page {
+                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
+                    let mut next = old.clone();
+                    let mut changed = false;
+                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
+                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
+                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
+                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
+                        }
+                    }
+                    if changed {
+                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
+                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(rewritten)
+    }

   870	    fn charge_source_indexes(&mut self, table: &Table, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>, mut entries: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   871	        for index in table.indexes.values() {
   872	            if let Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) = index.components.first() {
   873	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps() * (u64::from(old.is_some()) + u64::from(new.is_some())))?;
   874	            }
   875	        }
   876	        if self.maintain_prepaid {
   877	            let id = old.or(new).expect("source image").field("id")?.as_str()?;
   878	            for index in table.indexes.values() {
   879	                if matches!(index.components.first(), Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(_))) {
   880	                    let before = old.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   881	                    let after = new.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   882	                    let changed = before.iter().filter(|key| !after.contains(key)).count() + after.iter().filter(|key| !before.contains(key)).count();
   883	                    entries = entries.saturating_sub(changed as u64);
   884	                }
   885	            }
   886	        }
   887	        self.meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   888	        Ok(())
   889	    }

   981	        Value::String(s) | Value::Id(s) => format!("'{s}'"),
   982	        other => canonical_json(other),

   170	that null group is never counted in the action reservation and the inference
   171	never proves a table population bound. When both declarations exist, the
   172	effective bound is the smaller of the explicit cap and one.
   173	
   174	### 2.3 The reference index
   175	
   176	Every reference whose action probes or writes its children is probed by its
   177	column. The binder reuses a plain index whose leading columns are the
   178	reference (then, for an expiring child, its **effective** deadline column: a
   179	`read through` child's captured `$deadline`, which is the earlier of its own
   180	and its parents' deadlines, else its `expire at` column); otherwise it
   181	synthesizes an engine-named one: `[column, id]`, or
   182	`[column, deadlineColumn, id]` for an expiring child, so one seek skips
   183	an expired backlog (as `read through`'s child index does, LLP 3000.014 §6):
   184	the live rows are exactly `[id, null]` (never expires) and `[id]` with the
   185	deadline after now, so both seeks start at the live suffix and no expired row
   186	is ever visited.
   187	A `read through` reference uses its existing child index. The same index
   188	serves `cap N by <column>`. A `keep` reference gets none.
   189	
   190	## 3. What a delete does
   191	
   192	A delete of row `p` of table `P` — `delete P[id]`, `delete row`, a unique-key
   193	`delete P[key = …]`, a job, `POST /seed`'s delete, or `snapback4 data` —
   194	runs these steps in the deleting transaction, on every host:
   195	
   196	1. **Find and authorize `p`**, as today, with one addition: when any
   197	   `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` reference names `P`, the caller needs
   198	   **read authority on `p`** as well as delete authority, for every delete
   199	   attempt, with or without children. A caller who may delete but not read
   200	   gets the ordinary hidden-target refusal. This is LLP 3000.014 §3.1's
   201	   rule, generalized from `read through` children to every referenced table,
   202	   and it keeps step 3 from probing a hidden row's children. The system
   203	   principal passes both rules, as it does every rule.
   204	2. **Reserve.** Charge the reservation `R(P)` of §5.1 on every meter, draw
   205	   its row count from the request's physical authorization allowance, and
   206	   publish the schema-fixed trace of §4.2.
   207	3. **Close.** Starting from `p`, follow every `cascade` reference to the
   208	   live rows that reference a reached row, and repeat: the **closure** `S`
   209	   is `p` plus every row reached. (`S` is finite: the cascade graph is
   210	   acyclic and each edge has an explicit or inferred effective bound.) Steps 3–5 stream the referencing rows
   211	   through the reference index (§2.3) a bounded page at a time and keep only
   212	   identities; no image outlives its page.
   213	4. **Restrict.** For every row `s` in `S` and every `restrict` reference
   214	   into `s`'s table, look for a live row that references `s` **and is not
   215	   itself in `S`**: the probe streams past the rows of `S` that name `s` —
   216	   `p` included, which may name itself — to the first live row outside `S`
   217	   (each row of `S` names one target per reference, so a delete's probes
   218	   visit each row of `S` at most once, plus one witness per probe). Every
   219	   such probe runs. If any is occupied, refuse with
   220	   the **first occupied reference in schema order** of
   221	   `(child table, column)` — never the first found while walking hidden
   222	   rows:
   223	
   224	   `E_REFERENCED: projects at <site> is still referenced through comments.task (on delete restrict); delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)`
   225	
   226	   "Live" means present and not expired. A row inserted earlier in the same
   227	   transaction counts; one deleted earlier in it does not. Because rows in
   228	   `S` are excluded, a diamond (`A` cascades to `B` and `C`, and `C`
   229	   restricts `B`) or a self-referencing child table deletes when the whole
   230	   closure goes together, as SQL's statement-end `NO ACTION` does. A `read
   231	   through` reference is not part of this pass: it keeps its own refusal,
   232	   `E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN`, and its stricter physical-child probe (LLP
   233	   3000.014 §3.3), evaluated as each row of `S` is removed in step 6. When
   234	   both would refuse, `E_REFERENCED` comes first (step 4 runs before any
   235	   removal).
   236	5. **Set null.** For every row `s` in `S` and every `set null` reference into
   237	   `s`'s table, clear the column of each live referencing row **not in
   238	   `S`** (deletion dominates: a row that is going away is not rewritten).
   239	   Each reference's group is gathered whole (ids only, at most its effective
   240	   bound: the explicit cap or inferred one)
   241	   before any of it is cleared: a clear can recount a sibling whose
   242	   maintained column shares the reference's index and move it behind a page
   243	   cursor. The write rereads the row's current image immediately before clearing it
   244	   (an earlier clear's maintained write may have changed it), consults no
   245	   rule, and applies its constraints, maintains and partition events as any
   246	   write does.
   247	6. **Delete.** Remove the rows of `S` other than `p`, each table before every
   248	   table it must not outlive: its cascade parents and its `read through`
   249	   parent. Only those edges order the removal (an ordinary `restrict` or
   250	   `set null` reference between rows of `S` imposes none, since step 4
   251	   already cleared them), `check` refuses a cycle in their union
   252	   (`E_REFERENCE_ACTION`; e.g. `B` cascades from `P`, `C` cascades from `B`,
   253	   and `B` reads through `C`), and ties keep discovery order. Each row is
   254	   removed from its current image, consulting no rule and applying
   255	   constraints, maintains and partition events as any delete does. Then
   256	   remove `p` as today, **from its current image too**: the actions may have
   257	   changed it (a maintained column on `p` mirrors its children's removal), and
   258	   a store removes index entries from the image it is given. Authorization
   259	   stays the decision of step 1.
   260	
   261	Every step is inside the mutation's transaction: a refusal anywhere (a
   262	`restrict`, a read-through child, the meter) aborts the whole mutation, and
   263	nothing commits.
   264	
   265	An ordinary authored delete derives its closure and action witnesses from the
   266	logical unexpired store, then applies the resulting actions to the physical
   267	store. An expired child therefore neither blocks a `restrict` nor receives a
   268	`cascade` or `set null` action merely because cleanup has not removed its
   269	image yet.
   270	
   271	**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
   272	is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
   273	can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
   274	sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
   275	expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
   276	bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
   277	not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
   278	constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
   279	
   280	For an insert or upsert that reuses an expired predecessor's id, insert
   281	authority is evaluated against the pre-retirement logical store. The engine
   282	then retires the predecessor through the action path before the remaining
   283	uniqueness checks and physical insertion. At mutation commit, every row born
   284	or updated into an expired final image is retired through that same path. A
   285	refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
   286	earlier cascade and set-null writes.
   287	
   288	This commit-end rule also covers a source of a row-keyed maintained view. The
   289	source's final image first reaches normal maintenance, then its expired image
   290	is retired through the common action path in the same transaction. No derived
   291	maintenance shortcut may physically remove that source before closure
   292	preflight: doing so would bypass a live `restrict` child and could orphan a
   293	`cascade` or `set null` child. The source contribution and its retirement
   294	cancel within the transaction, so an already-expired birth never enters a
   295	committed count basis. The execution retains at most one retirement key per
   296	changed source row; its allocation is charged when first retained and the
   297	program's existing rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
   298	
   299	A live `restrict` child, or a physically retained read-through child outside
   300	the cascade closure but below a row in it, keeps the expired root physically
   301	stored and the sweep continues to later due keys. A read-through child inside
   302	the closure is removed first and is not a blocker. The action walk preflights
   303	both kinds of blocker before its first set-null or cascade write. The retained
   304	root remains logically unreadable.
   305	Short sweeps preserve both a per-table row continuation and a rotating table

+++ b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+import Quarry.Store
+
+/-!
+# Maintained aggregate identity
+
+The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
+tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
+cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
+store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
+lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
+and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
+identity while publishing the new version.
+-/
+
+namespace Quarry
+
+/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
+migration. -/
+def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
+
+/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
+not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
+to this logical model. -/
+def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
+  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
+    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
+    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble
+
+theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
+  simp [maintainedIdV1]
+
+/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
+byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
+theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
+  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
+  omega
+
+def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
+  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }
+
+structure MaintainedState where
+  version : Nat
+  rows : List Row
+
+/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
+identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
+states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
+def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
+    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
+  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
+example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
+  maintainedIdV1_length _
+
+end Quarry

+/-- Whether a row remains before its table's upper read lifetime. Null has no
+upper bound; the checked schema guarantees that a non-null value is a time. -/
+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — upper read lifetimes filter every logical read before physical cleanup.
+def unexpired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
+  match td.expire with
+  | none => true
+  | some c => match r.get c with
+    | .null => true
+    | .int closes => now < closes

+
+/-- Referential actions ignore expired child images but still govern a child
+whose lower read lifetime has not opened yet, matching the physical engine. -/
+def unexpiredStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
+  match sch.table? t with
+  | some td => (s t).filter (unexpired td now)
+  | none => []
+
+/-- The physical store with rows outside their logical lifetime removed. Rule
+probes use this store too, so a future or expired row cannot authorize work. -/
 def openedStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
   match sch.table? t with
-  | some td => (s t).filter (opened td now)
+  | some td => (s t).filter (live td now)
   | none => []

+  | some td => live td now r && td.read.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some r }

+/-- Apply actions to the physical store using only the rows that are logically
+live as action witnesses. The root may itself be absent from `witnesses`. -/
+def refDeleteFrom (sch : Schema) (witnesses physical : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
+  let cl := closure sch witnesses (storeSize sch witnesses + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
+  if restricted sch witnesses cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
+  else
+    let physical := cl.foldl (fun s (parent, row) => (referencing sch parent).foldl (fun s (child, col, action) =>
+      if action == .setNull then
+        ((witnesses child).filter fun k => names k col row.id && !inClosure cl child k).foldl
+          (fun s k => s.replaceRow child k (clearCol k col)) s
+      else s) s) physical
+    pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) physical)
+
+/-! ## Expiry retirement (LLP 3000.036.003 §6; LLP 3000.039 §3) -/
+
+def expired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
+  match td.expire with
+  | none => false
+  | some c => match r.get c with
+    | .int closes => closes <= now
+    | _ => false
+
+def stored (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
+  (s t).any fun current => current.id == r.id
+
+/-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
+stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
+model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
+root can be retired immediately. -/
+def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
+  sch.tables.foldl (fun s td => (s td.name).foldl (fun s r =>
+    if expired td now r && stored s td.name r then
+      match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s td.name r with
+      | .ok next => next
+      | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => s
+      | .error _ => s
+    else s) s) s
+
 /-- Apply one write to the store. -/

+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — born-expired and updated-expired final images retire in the writer transaction.
+/-- Rows whose final images a mutation changed. Commit-end expiry retirement
+is scoped to this set; pre-existing expired backlog remains for the ordinary
+sweep. -/
+abbrev ChangedRows := List (String × List Nat)
+
+structure MutationWorld where
+  store : Store
+  changed : ChangedRows := []
+
+def RWrite.explicitId? : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)
+  | .insert t fields _ => match fields.lookup "id" with
+    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+    | _ => none
+  | .upsert t key patch =>
+    match key.lookup "id" with
+    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+    | _ => match patch.lookup "id" with
+      | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
+      | _ => none
+  | _ => none
+
+def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=
+  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => (after td.name).filterMap fun row =>
+    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
+    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
+    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)
+
+def mutationHooks : Hooks MutationWorld where
+  view cx w := visibleRowsAt cx.schema w.store cx.viewer cx.now
+  apply cx w rw := match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
+    | .error e => .error e
+    | .ok (value, store) =>
+      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
+      let changed := match rw.explicitId? with | some address => changed ++ [address] | none => changed
+      .ok (value, { store, changed := changed.eraseDups })

+      | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest

+          let s ← refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t row
+          retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
+        else retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest

codex
The migration derives target-specific maps before rewriting typed references, then rebuilds targets under the writer transaction. I’m checking repeated sweeps next: the runtime carries row and table cursors between calls, so the formal ordering needs to account for that history.

+fn legacy_maintained_ids(schema: &Schema, rows: &[ReceiptRow]) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, String> {
+    let mut ids = BTreeMap::new();

+            Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}.id: {error}", receipt.table)),
+        };
+        let key = maintain.by.iter().map(|field| receipt.row.field(field).cloned().map_err(|error| format!("{}.{}: {error}", receipt.table, field))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
+        let new = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        if let Some(prior) = ids.insert(old.clone(), new.clone())
+            && prior != new
+        {
+            return Err(format!("legacy id {old} names more than one maintained group"));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(ids)
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_row(schema: &Schema, table: &str, row: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    if !schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.target == table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) { return; }
+    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return };
+    let Some(Value::Id(id)) = fields.get_mut("id") else { return };
+    if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+        *id = replacement.clone();
+    }
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_expected(expected: &mut Expected, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<(), String> {
+    if ids.is_empty() || expected.error_code.is_some() { return Ok(()); }
+    let Some(canonical) = &expected.canonical_result else { return Ok(()) };
+    let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(canonical).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    translate_legacy_maintained_result(&mut value, ids);
+    expected.canonical_result = Some(snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&value));
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_result(value: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    match value {
+        Value::Id(id) => {
+            if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+                *id = replacement.clone();
+            }
+        }
+        Value::Array(values) => values.iter_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}

    21	    let backend = plain();

    25	    let mut future = serde_json::to_value(&backend).unwrap();

    75	fn legacy_digest_store<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S) -> Backend {
    76	    let source = "table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n";
    77	    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
    78	    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
    79	    let mut current = Backend { generation: 2, schema: bound.schema, programs: bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program).collect() };
    80	    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&current).unwrap();
    81	    legacy["generation"] = json!(1);
    82	    for table in legacy["schema"]["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
    83	        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
    84	            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
    85	                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
    86	            }
    87	        }
    88	    }
    89	    let old: Backend = serde_json::from_value(legacy.clone()).unwrap();
    90	    store.install(&old.schema, &BTreeMap::from([
    91	        ("device:backend".into(), legacy.to_string()),
    92	        ("device:generation".into(), "1".into()),
    93	    ]), false).unwrap();
    94	    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
    95	    tx.outbox_insert(1, "pending", r#"{"id":"pending","seq":1,"op":"write","args":{},"new_ids":[]}"#).unwrap();
    96	    tx.commit().unwrap();
    97	    current.generation = 2;
    98	    current
    99	}

   101	fn legacy_digest_recovery<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S, initial: bool) {
   102	    let current = legacy_digest_store(store);
   103	    let error = match Opening::Kept.open(Borrowed(store)) {
   104	        Err(error) => error,
   105	        Ok(_) => panic!("offline device executed a kept pre-digest backend"),
   106	    };
   107	    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
   108	    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
   109	    let before = tx.outbox_entries().unwrap();
   110	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   111	    let opening = if initial { Opening::Initial(current) } else { Opening::Install(current) };
   112	    drop(opening.open(Borrowed(store)).expect("a current backend must recover a kept legacy backend"));
   113	    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
   114	    assert_eq!(tx.outbox_entries().unwrap(), before, "semantic upgrade preserves queued writes");
   115	    assert_eq!(tx.meta("device:generation").unwrap().as_deref(), Some("2"));
   116	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   117	}

   134	// Borrow the real store so a refused opening leaves it available for inspection.
   135	struct Borrowed<'a, S>(&'a mut S);
   136	impl<S: DeviceStore> DeviceStore for Borrowed<'_, S> {
   137	    type Tx<'a> = S::Tx<'a> where Self: 'a;
   138	    fn install(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   139	        self.0.install(schema, metadata, reset)
   140	    }
   141	    fn install_checked(&mut self, schema: &Schema, metadata: &BTreeMap<String, String>, reset: bool, expected: &BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   142	        self.0.install_checked(schema, metadata, reset, expected)
   143	    }
   144	    fn meta(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> { self.0.meta(key) }
   145	    fn set_meta(&mut self, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> { self.0.set_meta(key, value) }
   146	    fn transaction(&mut self) -> Result<Self::Tx<'_>, RuntimeError> { self.0.transaction() }
   147	}

   149	fn refused_reopen_preserves<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S) {
   150	    let backend = plain();
   151	    drop(Device::open_store(Borrowed(store), Some(backend.clone())).unwrap());
   152	    let row = object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into()))]);
   153	    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
   154	    tx.put("t", &backend.schema.tables["t"], &row, None).unwrap();
   155	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   156	    let mut future = serde_json::to_value(&backend).unwrap();
   157	    future["schema"]["tables"]["t"]["constraints"] = json!([{"Capabilities":["future-derivation"]}]);
   158	    store.set_meta("device:backend", &future.to_string()).unwrap();
   159	    let mut replacement = backend;
   160	    replacement.generation = 2; // Without the fence this resets the held row.
   161	    let before = store.transaction().unwrap().meta_prefix("").unwrap();
   162	    for opening in [Opening::Install(replacement.clone()), Opening::Kept, Opening::Initial(replacement)] {
   163	        let error = match opening.open(Borrowed(store)) {
   164	            Err(error) => error,
   165	            Ok(_) => panic!("unsupported kept backend accepted during reopening"),
   166	        };
   167	        assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
   168	        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
   169	        assert_eq!(tx.meta_prefix("").unwrap(), before, "refusal must preserve all metadata");
   170	        assert_eq!(tx.get("t", "kept").unwrap(), Some(row.clone()), "refusal must preserve rows");
   171	    }
   172	}

   191	// Linux counterpart of schema-capabilities.test.mjs's published-engine fence.
   192	// Include DDL (indexes/triggers/columns), every table and every stored value.
   193	// The refusal contract covers schema/rows, integrity and freelist count.
   194	// WAL identity is asserted for the small no-spill cases below; a large rolled
   195	// back migration may change free-page contents or retain uncommitted frames
   196	// (LLP 3000.033 §1.3).
   197	fn sqlite_dump(path: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> {
   198	    let db = rusqlite::Connection::open_with_flags(path, rusqlite::OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY).unwrap();
   199	    let mut tables = vec!["sqlite_schema".to_string()];
   200	    tables.extend(db.prepare("SELECT name FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name").unwrap()
   201	        .query_map([], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0)).unwrap().map(Result::unwrap));
   202	    let mut snapshot = tables.into_iter().map(|name| {
   203	        let mut stmt = db.prepare(&format!("SELECT * FROM \"{}\"", name.replace('"', "\"\""))).unwrap();
   204	        let columns = stmt.column_count();
   205	        let mut rows = stmt.query_map([], |r| (0..columns).map(|i| r.get::<_, rusqlite::types::Value>(i)).collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>())
   206	            .unwrap().map(|r| format!("{:?}", r.unwrap())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   207	        rows.sort();
   208	        (name, rows)
   209	    }).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   210	    let integrity: String = db.query_row("PRAGMA integrity_check", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
   211	    assert_eq!(integrity, "ok");
   212	    let free: i64 = db.query_row("PRAGMA freelist_count", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
   213	    snapshot.push(("PRAGMA integrity_check/freelist_count".into(), vec![integrity, free.to_string()]));
   214	    snapshot
   215	}

   217	fn legacy_device(path: &std::path::Path, mode: &str) {
   218	    drop(snapback4_device::native::Device::open(path, Some(plain())).unwrap());
   219	    let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(path).unwrap();
   220	    db.execute("INSERT INTO r(t,id,data) SELECT num,'kept',?1 FROM _catalog WHERE name = 't'",
   221	        [serde_json::to_string(&object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into()))])).unwrap()]).unwrap();
   222	    db.execute_batch("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _read_sessions;").unwrap();
   223	    let has_scope: bool = db.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('_session_mint_bindings') WHERE name = 'scope')", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
   224	    if has_scope { db.execute_batch("ALTER TABLE _session_mint_bindings DROP COLUMN scope;").unwrap(); }
   225	    db.execute_batch(&format!("PRAGMA journal_mode = {mode};")).unwrap();
   226	}

   230	    future.generation = 2;
   231	    future.schema.tables.get_mut("t").unwrap().constraints.push(
   232	        snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Capabilities(["future-derivation".into()].into()));
   233	    future
   234	}

   251	        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cascade")), ("message", id("message"))])),

     1	//! A store written by the frozen 0.4.28 binary adopts digest-addressed
     2	//! aggregate rows before the current engine serves it.
     3	use rusqlite::Connection;
     4	use std::{
     5	    fs,
     6	    path::{Path, PathBuf},
     7	    process::Command,

    10	const BASELINE_SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
    11	table groups:
    12	  owner: principal
    13	  immutable owner
    14	  insert <- allow
    15	  public
    16	table entries:
    17	  group: text <=256
    18	  ownerGroup: groups
    19	  amount: int
    20	  immutable ownerGroup
    21	  insert <- allow
    22	  public
    23	view totals: sum entries of .amount by .group
    24	  public
    25	table pointers:
    26	  total: totals
    27	  insert <- allow
    28	  public
    29	view pointerTotals: count pointers by .total
    30	  public
    31	table saved:
    32	  target: pointerTotals
    33	  insert <- allow
    34	  public
    35	mutation createGroup(id: id, owner: principal):
    36	  insert groups {id, owner}
    37	mutation add(group: text <=256, ownerGroup: groups, amount: int):
    38	  insert entries {group, ownerGroup, amount}
    39	mutation point(total: totals):
    40	  insert pointers {total}
    41	mutation save(target: pointerTotals):
    42	  insert saved {target}
    43	query total(group: text <=256):
    44	  return totals[group]
    45	"#;
    46	
    47	const SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
    48	table groups:
    49	  owner: principal
    50	  immutable owner
    51	  insert <- allow
    52	  public
    53	table entries:
    54	  group: text <=256
    55	  ownerGroup: groups
    56	  amount: int
    57	  immutable ownerGroup
    58	  insert <- allow
    59	  public
    60	view totals: sum entries of .amount by .group
    61	  public
    62	view ownerTotals: count entries by .ownerGroup.owner
    63	  public
    64	table pointers:
    65	  total: totals
    66	  insert <- allow
    67	  public
    68	view pointerTotals: count pointers by .total
    69	  public
    70	table saved:
    71	  target: pointerTotals
    72	  insert <- allow
    73	  public
    74	mutation createGroup(id: id, owner: principal):
    75	  insert groups {id, owner}
    76	mutation add(group: text <=256, ownerGroup: groups, amount: int):
    77	  insert entries {group, ownerGroup, amount}
    78	mutation point(total: totals):
    79	  insert pointers {total}
    80	mutation save(target: pointerTotals):
    81	  insert saved {target}
    82	query total(group: text <=256):
    83	  return totals[group]
    84	"#;
    85	
    86	const CHAIN_SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
    87	table links:
    88	  previous: chain ?
    89	  insert <- allow
    90	  public
    91	view chain: count links by .previous
    92	  public
    93	table saved:
    94	  target: chain
    95	  insert <- allow
    96	  public
    97	mutation add(previous: chain ?):
    98	  insert links {previous}
    99	mutation save(target: chain):
   100	  insert saved {target}
   101	query count(previous: chain ?):
   102	  return chain[previous]
   103	"#;
   104	
   105	struct Temp(PathBuf);
   106	impl Temp {
   107	    fn new(source: &str) -> Self {
   108	        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
   109	            "snapback4-maintained-id-{}-{}",
   110	            std::process::id(),
   111	            std::time::SystemTime::now()
   112	                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
   113	                .unwrap()
   114	                .as_nanos()
   115	        ));
   116	        fs::create_dir_all(path.join("snapback")).unwrap();
   117	        fs::write(path.join("snapback/schema.q"), source).unwrap();
   118	        Self(path)
   119	    }
   120	}
   121	impl Drop for Temp {
   122	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   123	        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
   124	    }
   125	}
   126	
   127	fn aggregate_id(store: &Path) -> String {
   128	    Connection::open(store)
   129	        .unwrap()
   130	        .query_row(
   131	            "SELECT r.id FROM r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t WHERE c.name='totals'",
   132	            [],
   133	            |row| row.get(0),
   134	        )
   135	        .unwrap()
   136	}
